children.title: Linearization Route
children.top_down_role: Replacement of difficult coupled subproblems by tractable approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous proximal linearization for a convex–concave saddle function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a saddle function \(\mathcal L(x,y)=f(x)+\Phi(x,y)-g(y)\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proximable and \(\Phi\) is differentiable, choose \(x^0\), \(y^0\), and stepsizes \(\tau,\sigma>0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\bigl(x^k-\tau\nabla_x\Phi(x^k,y^k)\bigr),
\qquad
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g}\bigl(y^k+\sigma\nabla_y\Phi(x^k,y^k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when a prescribed primal–dual residual or successive-iterate tolerance is met, and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). Each difficult coupled subproblem is thereby replaced by first-order models of \(\Phi\) and separate proximal evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the smooth coupling at the current primal–dual point, then apply separate proximal descent and ascent steps until a chosen residual tolerance is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex and proximable.
\(\Phi\) is differentiable, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration uses only partial gradients of \(\Phi\) and separate proximal maps of \(f\) and \(g\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration is a plausible simultaneous proximal gradient descent-ascent scheme, but no source is supplied, the domains of f, g, Phi, x, and y are not declared, and no stepsize assumptions support a convergence interpretation. Moreover, an algorithm with an ad hoc stopping rule does not cleanly match a derivation-route container without a source tying this exact construction to the named route.

children.title: Arrow–Hurwicz Method Family
children.top_down_role: Explicit saddle dynamics and the corrections leading to stable proximal primal–dual methods.

children.title: Basic Arrow–Hurwicz Method
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous explicit primal and dual evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Arrow–Hurwicz Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit simultaneous descent–ascent for a differentiable saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal L:\mathcal H\times\mathcal G\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, convex in its first argument, and concave in its second. Choose \((x^0,y^0)\) and stepsizes \(\tau,
\sigma>0\). The basic Arrow–Hurwicz iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau\nabla_x\mathcal L(x^k,y^k),
\qquad
y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma\nabla_y\mathcal L(x^k,y^k).
\]
Both updates use the same current pair, so the method is simultaneous explicit gradient descent–ascent. Stop when the saddle-gradient residual \(\lVert(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x^k,y^k),-\nabla_y\mathcal L(x^k,y^k))\rVert\) is below a prescribed tolerance, and return the current pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arrow–Hurwicz simultaneously takes an explicit gradient descent step in the primal variable and an explicit gradient ascent step in the dual variable.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(\mathcal L\) is differentiable, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates follow simultaneous explicit primal descent and dual ascent with the stated residual-based output rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind and the simultaneous descent-ascent update matches the container. The formula is mathematically clear, but no authoritative locator supports the exact Arrow-Hurwicz variant or its residual-based output rule; the stated convex-concave assumptions alone also do not imply convergence for arbitrary positive stepsizes.

children.title: Proximal Arrow–Hurwicz Variants
children.top_down_role: Implicit treatment of nonsmooth primal or dual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Arrow–Hurwicz Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit nonsmooth primal and dual steps for a bilinear saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{x\in\mathcal H}\max_{y\in\mathcal G}
\bigl\{f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\bigr\},
\]
choose \((x^0,y^0)\) and \(\tau,\sigma>0\). A simultaneous proximal Arrow–Hurwicz variant computes
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^k),
\qquad
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma Kx^k).
\]
Stop when the fixed-point residual formed from these two proximal updates is below a prescribed tolerance, and return the current pair. The proximal maps treat the nonsmooth subdifferentials implicitly, while the bilinear coupling remains explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal Arrow–Hurwicz step handles nonsmooth primal and dual terms through separate proximal maps while evaluating the bilinear coupling explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex and proximable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed simultaneous iteration implicitly treats \(\partial f\) and \(\partial g^*\) and explicitly treats \(K\) and \(K^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal simultaneous update fits the algorithmic leaf and correctly distinguishes implicit nonsmooth terms from explicit bilinear coupling. A source is required to identify this exact update as a proximal Arrow-Hurwicz variant and to support the fixed-point stopping rule and any intended stepsize regime.

children.title: Extragradient-Extrapolation Correction Family
children.top_down_role: Corrections for explicit saddle instability.

children.title: Extragradient Corrections
children.top_down_role: Extra-evaluation corrections for explicit saddle dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Extragradient Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-evaluation correction for a monotone Lipschitz inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal Z\rightrightarrows\mathcal Z\) be maximally monotone and let \(F:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\) be monotone and Lipschitz continuous. Choose \(z^0\in\mathcal Z\) and \(\gamma>0\). The forward–backward extragradient correction is
\[
w^k=J_{\gamma A}(z^k-\gamma Fz^k),
\qquad
z^{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}(z^k-\gamma Fw^k).
\]
The first point predicts a resolvent step, and the second reevaluates the explicit operator at that prediction. Stop when \(\lVert z^k-w^k\rVert/\gamma\) is below a prescribed tolerance, and return \(w^k\) or the final corrected iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient splitting predicts a resolvent point, reevaluates the monotone explicit operator there, and performs a corrected resolvent step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each corrected iteration uses two evaluations of \(F\) and two resolvent evaluations of \(A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed two-resolvent predictor-corrector is a mathematically definable extragradient-type algorithm, but it is not the usual one-resolvent forward-backward-forward formula. A specific source is needed to establish the intended variant, its assumptions and stepsize range, and whether the returned point is the predictor or corrected iterate.

children.title: Extrapolation Corrections
children.top_down_role: Predictive corrections based on extrapolated primal or dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolation Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal extrapolation correction in a proximal primal–dual scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the saddle problem associated with \(f(x)+g(Kx)\), choose \(x^0\), \(y^0\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and select \(\tau,
\sigma>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\). Iterate
\[
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),
\]
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),
\qquad
\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).
\]
Stop when the primal and dual fixed-point residuals meet prescribed tolerances, and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). The extrapolated primal point supplies the correction used by the next dual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scheme forms a proximal dual step, a proximal primal step, and an extrapolated primal point that corrects the next dual evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex and proximable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correction is \(\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k)\), which enters the subsequent dual proximal step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed updates match a standard primal-extrapolated proximal primal-dual pattern and algorithm is the proper kind. However, the spaces and function domains are omitted, and no source supports the exact ordering, parameter range, stopping rule, or usual coupling condition.

children.title: Correction-Based Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Stability changes attributable to the correction mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction-Based Stability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient stepsize regimes for extragradient and extrapolated corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In finite dimensions, two standard correction-based stability regimes are as follows. For the projected extragradient method on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), with monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz map \(F\) and a nonempty solution set, choose
\[
0<\gamma<1/L.
\]
For the extrapolated proximal primal–dual iteration with \(\theta=1\), bounded linear \(K\), proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(f,g\), and an existing saddle point, choose
\[
\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1.
\]
Under the respective condition, the correction controls the explicit coupling and the generated iterates converge to a variational-inequality solution or a primal–dual saddle point, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient is stable below the reciprocal Lipschitz threshold; the standard extrapolated proximal primal–dual scheme is stable when the primal–dual stepsize product is below the coupling threshold.
assumptions_latex: The relevant solution set is nonempty.
The operators and functions satisfy the monotonicity, Lipschitz, convexity, and closedness conditions stated above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sufficient regimes are \(0<\gamma<1/L\) and \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) for the respective corrected methods.

notation.meaning: operator norm of the coupling map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct content kind and both inequalities are recognizable sufficient regimes for particular standard methods. Sources are essential because the first regime is stated for projected extragradient while the sibling algorithm uses a general two-resolvent inclusion, and because convergence hypotheses and strict-versus-nonstrict endpoint conventions depend on the exact variants.

children.title: Saddle-Dynamics Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure modes of uncorrected descent–ascent.

children.title: Persistent Oscillation Patterns
children.top_down_role: Cycling or sustained oscillation in uncorrected descent–ascent dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Oscillation Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergent periodic behavior of uncorrected continuous-time saddle dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the bilinear saddle function \(\mathcal L(x,y)=xy\) on \(\mathbb R^2\). Its continuous-time Arrow–Hurwicz dynamics are
\[
\dot x(t)=-y(t),
\qquad
\dot y(t)=x(t).
\]
For initial condition \((x(0),y(0))=(a,b)\), the trajectory is
\[
x(t)=a\cos t-b\sin t,
\qquad
y(t)=a\sin t+b\cos t.
\]
Consequently, \(x(t)^2+y(t)^2=a^2+b^2\) for every \(t\). Unless \((a,b)=(0,0)\), the trajectory is periodic and never converges to the unique saddle point, showing that convexity–concavity alone does not damp saddle dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bilinear saddle, continuous descent–ascent rotates on circles of constant radius, producing perpetual oscillation rather than convergence to the saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trajectory is periodic with constant radius \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\) and does not converge to \((0,0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuous-time calculation is internally consistent, plain text matches the equations, and counterexample is the exact mathematical role for this failure-pattern leaf. No inspectable source or locator is supplied, so it cannot enter candidate-review knowledge under the evidence rules.

children.title: Divergent Saddle Dynamics
children.top_down_role: Unbounded or nonconvergent behavior of explicit saddle iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergent Saddle Dynamics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric divergence of simultaneous explicit descent–ascent on a bilinear saddle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathcal L(x,y)=xy\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), apply simultaneous Arrow–Hurwicz updates with a common stepsize \(\gamma>0\):
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x^{k+1}\\y^{k+1}\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}1&-\gamma\\\gamma&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x^k\\y^k\end{pmatrix}.
\]
A direct norm calculation gives
\[
(x^{k+1})^2+(y^{k+1})^2=(1+\gamma^2)\bigl((x^k)^2+(y^k)^2\bigr).
\]
Thus every nonzero initial point satisfies \(\lVert(x^k,y^k)\rVert=(1+\gamma^2)^{k/2}\lVert(x^0,y^0)\rVert\), so the iterates diverge for every positive constant stepsize despite the existence of the saddle point \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous explicit descent–ascent on a bilinear saddle expands the iterate norm by a fixed factor greater than one at every step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(x^k,y^k)\rVert=(1+\gamma^2)^{k/2}\lVert(x^0,y^0)\rVert\to+\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix update and geometric norm growth are correct for simultaneous explicit descent-ascent on the bilinear saddle, and counterexample is the correct content kind. No inspectable source or locator is supplied, so the record requires evidence before candidate-review acceptance.

children.title: Stepsize Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter thresholds separating stable behavior from instability.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp spectral instability boundary for simultaneous explicit Arrow–Hurwicz updates on a bilinear saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:X\to Y\) be a nonzero linear map between finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, and consider \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\langle Kx,y\rangle\). The simultaneous Arrow–Hurwicz iteration is \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau K^*y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma Kx^k.\] For any singular value \(s>0\) of \(K\), the iteration matrix restricted to the corresponding singular mode has eigenvalues \(1\pm i\sqrt{\tau\sigma}\,s\) when \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma>0\), and hence spectral radius \(\sqrt{1+\tau\sigma s^2}>1\). Thus no strictly positive stepsize pair is linearly stable on this problem. The equality \(\tau\sigma=0\) is only the spectral-radius boundary: if exactly one stepsize is zero, the resulting shear can still fail to be power-bounded; the trivial choice \(\tau=\sigma=0\) is stationary, while nontrivial stable behavior requires a modified update such as an implicit or extragradient scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nontrivial bilinear saddle problem, simultaneous explicit primal–dual gradient steps are spectrally unstable for every positive primal and dual stepsize. Setting only one stepsize to zero reaches spectral radius one but does not generally produce a power-bounded iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma>0\), \(\rho(M)>1\) on every positive singular mode; \(\tau\sigma=0\) is a spectral-radius boundary but is not by itself sufficient for power-bounded stability.

notation.meaning: A positive singular value of K

children.title: Chambolle–Pock Algorithm
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual hybrid gradient family for linearly coupled saddle problems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of the Chambolle–Pock iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convergence under saddle-point existence, full extrapolation, and the strict step-size condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that the associated saddle problem has a saddle point. Choose \(\theta=1\) and \(\sigma,\tau>0\) such that \(\tau\sigma\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}^{2}<1\). If \((x^n,\bar x^n,\xi^n)\) is generated by \((\mathrm{PD}_1)-(\mathrm{PD}_3)\), then \((x^n,\xi^n)\) converges to a saddle point \((x^\sharp,\xi^\sharp)\). In particular, \(x^n\) converges to a minimizer of the primal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a saddle point exists, full extrapolation is used, and the strict step-size bound holds, the primal–dual iterates converge to a saddle point and the primal iterates converge to a primal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^n,\xi^n)\to(x^\sharp,\xi^\sharp)\in\operatorname{Saddle}(L),\qquad x^n\to x^\sharp\in\operatorname*{argmin}\text{(primal problem)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed points characterize Chambolle–Pock saddle points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between fixed points of the three-step primal–dual iteration and primal–dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\theta\in[0,1]\), a pair \((x^\sharp,\xi^\sharp)\) is a fixed point of the Chambolle–Pock updates \((\mathrm{PD}_1)-(\mathrm{PD}_3)\) if and only if it is a saddle point of the associated saddle formulation, equivalently a primal–dual optimal pair for the associated primal and dual problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every allowed extrapolation parameter, the fixed points of the Chambolle–Pock iteration are exactly the saddle points and hence the associated primal–dual optimal pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^\sharp,\xi^\sharp)\text{ is a fixed point}\iff(x^\sharp,\xi^\sharp)\text{ is a saddle point, equivalently a primal--dual optimal pair.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cumulative Chambolle–Pock primal–dual gap estimate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon energy and increment estimate under full extrapolation and the algorithm's strict step-size condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^n,\bar x^n,\xi^n)_{n\ge0}\) be generated by \((\mathrm{PD}_1)-(\mathrm{PD}_3)\) with \(\theta=1\), and let \(x\in\mathbb C^N\), \(\xi\in\mathbb C^m\) be arbitrary. For every \(M\ge1\), \[\begin{aligned}\sum_{n=1}^{M}\bigl(L(x^n,\xi)-L(x,\xi^n)\bigr)&+\frac{\lVert x-x^M\rVert_2^2}{2\tau}+\frac{1-\sigma\tau\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}^2}{2\sigma}\lVert\xi-\xi^M\rVert_2^2\\&+\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}}{2\tau}\sum_{n=1}^{M-1}\lVert x^n-x^{n-1}\rVert_2^2\\&+\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}}{2\sigma}\sum_{n=1}^{M}\lVert\xi^n-\xi^{n-1}\rVert_2^2\\&\le\frac{\lVert x-x^0\rVert_2^2}{2\tau}+\frac{\lVert\xi-\xi^0\rVert_2^2}{2\sigma}.\end{aligned}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under full extrapolation and the strict step-size bound, the cumulative primal–dual gap, terminal distance terms, and weighted sums of primal and dual increments are bounded by the initial weighted distances for every finite iteration horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{n=1}^{M}(L(x^n,\xi)-L(x,\xi^n))+\frac{\lVert x-x^M\rVert_2^2}{2\tau}+\frac{1-\sigma\tau\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}^2}{2\sigma}\lVert\xi-\xi^M\rVert_2^2+\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}}{2\tau}\sum_{n=1}^{M-1}\lVert x^n-x^{n-1}\rVert_2^2+\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}}{2\sigma}\sum_{n=1}^{M}\lVert\xi^n-\xi^{n-1}\rVert_2^2\le\frac{\lVert x-x^0\rVert_2^2}{2\tau}+\frac{\lVert\xi-\xi^0\rVert_2^2}{2\sigma}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chambolle–Pock primal–dual iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual proximal iteration for convex functions linearly coupled by a complex matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), convex functions \(F,G\), \(\theta\in[0,1]\), and \(\tau,\sigma>0\) satisfying \(\tau\sigma\lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}^{2}<1\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb C^N\), \(\xi^0\in\mathbb C^m\), and \(\bar x^0=x^0\). Iterate \(\xi^{n+1}=P_{F^*}(\sigma;\xi^n+\sigma A\bar x^n)\), \(x^{n+1}=P_G(\tau;x^n-\tau A^*\xi^{n+1})\), and \(\bar x^{n+1}=x^{n+1}+\theta(x^{n+1}-x^n)\). At the stopping index \(\bar n\), output \(\xi^\sharp=\xi^{\bar n}\) and \(x^\sharp=x^{\bar n}\) as the dual and primal approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate the proximal mappings of the conjugate dual function and the primal function, then extrapolate the primal iterate. The algorithm reports the terminating dual and primal iterates as approximations; this algorithm statement alone does not guarantee their accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \xi^\sharp:=\xi^{\bar n}\text{ and }x^\sharp:=x^{\bar n}\text{ are returned as the dual and primal approximations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-step Chambolle–Pock energy inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration comparison inequality for arbitrary primal and dual reference points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^n,\bar x^n,\xi^n)_{n\ge0}\) be generated by \((\mathrm{PD}_1)-(\mathrm{PD}_3)\), and let \(x\in\mathbb C^N\) and \(\xi\in\mathbb C^m\) be arbitrary. For every \(n\ge1\), \[\frac12\Delta_\sigma\lVert\xi-\xi^n\rVert_2^2+\frac12\Delta_\tau\lVert x-x^n\rVert_2^2+\frac\sigma2\lVert\Delta_\sigma\xi^n\rVert_2^2+\frac\tau2\lVert\Delta_\tau x^n\rVert_2^2\le L(x,\xi^n)-L(x^n,\xi)+\operatorname{Re}\langle A(x^n-\bar x^{n-1}),\xi-\xi^n\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, the discrete changes in the primal and dual squared distances plus the squared increment terms are bounded by a Lagrangian comparison term and an extrapolation-coupling term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac12\Delta_\sigma\lVert\xi-\xi^n\rVert_2^2+\frac12\Delta_\tau\lVert x-x^n\rVert_2^2+\frac\sigma2\lVert\Delta_\sigma\xi^n\rVert_2^2+\frac\tau2\lVert\Delta_\tau x^n\rVert_2^2\le L(x,\xi^n)-L(x^n,\xi)+\operatorname{Re}\langle A(x^n-\bar x^{n-1}),\xi-\xi^n\rangle.

knowledge_statements.title: Base Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned finite-dimensional PDHG for a convex composite saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X} g(x)+f(Kx)\), equivalently \(\min_x\max_y g(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-f^*(y)\), choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\), \(\theta\in[0,1]\), and \(x^0,y^0\), with \(\bar x^0=x^0\). Iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma f^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),\] \[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Stop under a prescribed residual or iteration rule and return the latest primal–dual pair. The standard scalar compatibility condition is \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PDHG alternates a dual proximal step, a primal proximal step, and optional primal extrapolation under a coupled stepsize bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces and \(K:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(f:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The saddle problem has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recurrence defines the base PDHG family; its iterates are returned subject to \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolated Primal–Dual Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG variants distinguished by extrapolation of a primal iterate before the dual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the PDHG saddle problem, select \(\tau,\sigma>0\), extrapolation parameters \(\theta_k\), and \(x^{-1}=x^0\). Form \(\bar x^k=x^k+\theta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\), then update \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma f^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}).\] Constant extrapolation uses \(\theta_k\equiv\theta\); adaptive variants prescribe \(\theta_k\) from curvature or stepsize updates. Stop by a chosen primal–dual residual rule and return \((x^k,y^k)\). The base Chambolle–Pock choice is recovered by \(\theta_k\equiv1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These variants feed an extrapolated primal point into the dual proximal update, with constant or iteration-dependent extrapolation parameters.
assumptions_latex: The base PDHG problem and proximal mappings are well defined.
\(\tau>0\), \(\sigma>0\), and the selected parameter schedule satisfies its convergence compatibility condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed extrapolation and proximal updates define an extrapolated primal–dual variant.

children.title: Relaxed Primal–Dual Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Primal–Dual Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krasnosel'skii–Mann relaxation applied to a convergent primal–dual fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\times Y\to X\times Y\) denote one complete admissible PDHG update, and initialize \(z^0=(x^0,y^0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute the provisional point \(\widehat z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), choose \(\rho_k>0\), and set \[z^{k+1}=z^k+\rho_k(\widehat z^{k+1}-z^k).\] Stop when \(\lVert Tz^k-z^k\rVert\) meets a prescribed tolerance, and return \(z^k\). If \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged, a standard admissible regime is \(0<\inf_k\rho_k\leq\sup_k\rho_k<1/\alpha\); \(\rho_k=1\) recovers the unrelaxed update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed variant moves only a parameterized fraction, or an admissible overrelaxed multiple, toward each provisional PDHG update.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is an \(\alpha\)-averaged primal–dual fixed-point map for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed iterates are Krasnosel'skii–Mann iterates of \(T\) and use \(\lVert Tz^k-z^k\rVert\) as a fixed-point residual.

children.title: Combined Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of extrapolation levels with relaxation choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for jointly extrapolated and relaxed primal–dual fixed-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each extrapolation parameter \(\theta\), let \(T_\theta\) be the complete extrapolated primal–dual update on an augmented state containing the required iterate history. A combined extrapolation–relaxation regime is admissible whenever \(T_\theta\) is \(\alpha_\theta\)-averaged in a specified positive-definite metric, \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\theta\neq\varnothing\), and the relaxation sequence satisfies \[0<\underline\rho\leq\rho_k\leq\overline\rho<1/\alpha_\theta.\] The combined iteration is \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\rho_k(T_\theta z^k-z^k)\). Thus extrapolation and relaxation cannot be selected independently: the admissible relaxation interval is determined by the averagedness constant of the extrapolated map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint extrapolation and relaxation are compatible when the extrapolated update is averaged and relaxation remains strictly below its averagedness-dependent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\rho_k(T_\theta z^k-z^k)\) lies in an admissible combined parameter regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise metric PDHG using positive diagonal primal and dual stepsize operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose positive-definite diagonal operators \(T:X\to X\) and \(\Sigma:Y\to Y\), initialize \(x^0,y^0\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). Iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{\Sigma^{-1}}_{f^*}(y^k+\Sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_g(x^k-TK^*y^{k+1}),\] \[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Stop by a prescribed residual rule and return \((x^k,y^k)\). A standard strict compatibility requirement is \(\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\), which reduces to \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) when \(T=\tau I\) and \(\Sigma=\sigma I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal preconditioning assigns coordinatewise primal and dual metrics while retaining a norm compatibility bound on the scaled coupling operator.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(\Sigma\) are self-adjoint, positive-definite, and diagonal.
The base convex saddle problem has a solution.

children.title: Block Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Block Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-metric PDHG with positive-definite within-block primal and dual preconditioners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\bigoplus_{j=1}^mX_j\) and \(Y=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nY_i\). Choose block-diagonal positive-definite operators \(T=\operatorname{diag}(T_1,\ldots,T_m)\) and \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_n)\). Starting from \(x^0,y^0\), perform the metric PDHG updates \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{\Sigma^{-1}}_{f^*}(y^k+\Sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_g(x^k-TK^*y^{k+1}),\] followed by the prescribed extrapolation. Stop by a residual rule and return the latest pair. Require \(\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\); diagonal preconditioning is the scalar-within-coordinate special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block preconditioning uses positive-definite metrics within variable blocks and controls the norm of the correspondingly scaled coupling operator.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) admit the displayed finite orthogonal block decompositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric proximal updates define block-preconditioned PDHG compatible with the chosen block decomposition.

children.title: Primal–Dual Scaling Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements for paired primal and dual metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Scaling Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric coupling condition equivalent to strong positivity of the primal–dual block preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded and linear, and let \(T:X\to X\) and \(\Sigma:Y\to Y\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive. Primal and dual scalings are strictly compatible with \(K\) when \[\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1.\] This condition is equivalent to strong positivity of the bounded self-adjoint block operator \[P=\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&\Sigma^{-1}\end{pmatrix}:X\times Y\to X\times Y.\] In scalar metrics \(T=\tau I\) and \(\Sigma=\sigma I\), where \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma>0\), the condition becomes \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\). The non-strict inequality describes the norm boundary and does not by itself imply strong positivity of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded, strongly positive primal and dual metrics are strictly compatible when the scaled coupling norm is below one; equivalently, the associated primal–dual block metric is strongly positive.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to X\) and \(\Sigma:Y\to Y\) are bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\iff P\) is strongly positive on \(X\times Y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Accelerated Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated PDHG schedule when the primal term has a known strong-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(g\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex with \(\gamma>0\). Choose \(\tau_0,\sigma_0>0\) satisfying \(\tau_0\sigma_0\lVert K\rVert^2<1\), initialize \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_k f^*}(y^k+\sigma_kK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau_k g}(x^k-\tau_kK^*y^{k+1}),\] \[\theta_k=(1+2\gamma\tau_k)^{-1/2},\quad \tau_{k+1}=\theta_k\tau_k,\quad \sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k/\theta_k,\quad \bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta_k(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Stop by a prescribed residual or iteration budget and return the latest pair. A dual-strongly-convex version follows by interchanging primal and dual roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known strong convexity drives a changing PDHG stepsize and extrapolation schedule that accelerates the corresponding primal or dual geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and \(\gamma\)-strongly convex for \(\gamma>0\).
\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and a saddle point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed curvature-dependent schedule defines a primal-strong-convexity accelerated PDHG variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Primal–Dual Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized dual-block PDHG with probability-corrected extrapolation for separable composite objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x g(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(K_ix)\), choose probabilities \(p_i>0\), sample \(i_k\) independently, and update only the selected dual block: \[y_{i_k}^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_{i_k}f_{i_k}^*}(y_{i_k}^k+\sigma_{i_k}K_{i_k}x^k),\qquad y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\quad(j\neq i_k).\] Set \(\Delta y^k=y^{k+1}-y^k\), then compute \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}\!\left(x^k-\tau K^*(y^k+P^{-1}\Delta y^k)\right),\] where \(P^{-1}\) scales block \(i\) by \(1/p_i\). Stop using a prescribed stochastic residual or budget and return the current or averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic primal–dual method updates a sampled dual block and uses probability correction in the coupled primal step.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and a saddle point exists.
The samples \(i_k\) are independent with \(\mathbb P(i_k=i)=p_i>0\).
The block stepsizes satisfy an admissible probability-weighted coupling bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probability-corrected recurrence defines a stochastic dual-block primal–dual variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coordinate Primal–Dual Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual splitting that activates selected coordinate blocks while retaining inactive block values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the state as \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\), let \(Tz\) be one full admissible primal–dual update, and choose a nonempty block set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define \[z_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}(Tz^k)_i,&i\in S_k,\\z_i^k,&i\notin S_k.\end{cases}\] The block set may be cyclic, essentially cyclic, or randomly sampled; any auxiliary coupled quantity must be updated consistently with the changed blocks. Stop using a prescribed block residual or iteration budget and return \(z^k\). For randomized activation, require every block to have positive selection probability and stepsizes compatible with the block coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and unbiasedness conditions for randomized primal–dual block activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the random dual-block sample at iteration \(k\), adapted to filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\), and define \(p_i^k=\mathbb P(i\in I_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\). An admissible sampling regime has persistent coverage \[p_i^k\geq p_{\min}>0\qquad\text{for every }i,k.\] If \(U_i^k\) is the proposed increment of block \(i\), the inverse-probability corrected increment \(\widehat U^k=\sum_{i\in I_k}U_i^k/p_i^k\) satisfies \[\mathbb E[\widehat U^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sum_{i=1}^nU_i^k.\] Independent, minibatch, and conditionally adaptive sampling fit this regime when these predicates and the method-specific stepsize bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admissible sampling gives every block persistent positive probability and uses inverse-probability correction when an unbiased full increment is required.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i^k\geq p_{\min}>0\) for every block and iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat U^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sum_{i=1}^nU_i^k\), and every block remains persistently sampleable.

children.title: Primal–Dual Stepsize Admissibility

children.title: Scalar Stepsize Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Stepsize Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard scalar admissibility condition for a primal–dual coupling operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded linear, and choose scalar primal and dual stepsizes \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma>0\). The strictly admissible scalar regime is
\[\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1.\]
Equivalently, the normalized coupling \(\sqrt{\sigma}K\sqrt{\tau}\) has operator norm strictly below one. This condition makes the standard block primal–dual metric positive definite and supplies a uniform margin for the usual nonexpansive or averaged-operator convergence argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scalar stepsizes are strictly admissible when their product times the squared coupling norm is below one.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are real Hilbert spaces and \(K\in\mathcal L(X,Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).

children.title: Matrix-Preconditioned Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Preconditioned Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-valued admissibility for block-preconditioned primal–dual splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X\) and \(\Sigma:Y\to Y\) be bounded, self-adjoint, strongly positive preconditioners. For a bounded linear coupling \(K:X\to Y\), the strict matrix-preconditioned regime is
\[\lVert \Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1.\]
Equivalently, the block operator
\[M=\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&\Sigma^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\]
is strongly positive. Thus blockwise or anisotropic steps may be used while controlling the coupling in the induced primal and dual metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual preconditioners are admissible when the correspondingly scaled coupling has norm below one.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are real Hilbert spaces and \(K\in\mathcal L(X,Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\), equivalently \(M\succ0\).

children.title: Adaptive Linesearch Calibration Regime
children.top_down_role: Local calibration without a predetermined global norm.

children.title: Adaptive Stepsize Calibration
children.top_down_role: Iteration-dependent scaling based on observed local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Stepsize Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent scalar calibration preserving a uniform admissibility margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\tau_k,\sigma_k)_{k\ge0}\) be positive stepsizes for a fixed bounded coupling \(K:X\to Y\). An admissibility-preserving adaptive calibration maintains constants \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(0<m\le M<\infty\) such that
\[\tau_k\sigma_k\lVert K\rVert^2\le1-\varepsilon,\qquad m\le\tau_k/\sigma_k\le M\quad\text{for every }k.\]
Consequently, adaptation may redistribute scale between primal and dual updates without approaching degeneracy or crossing the scalar coupling boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive primal and dual steps may vary if their coupling product retains a uniform margin and their ratio remains bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k\tau_k\sigma_k\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) with uniformly controlled metric imbalance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounds describe a plausible uniformly safeguarded scalar adaptation, but they are not a universal characterization of adaptive primal–dual calibration. A source identifying the applicable adaptive scheme and its required metric-variation hypotheses is needed.

children.title: Linesearch Calibration
children.top_down_role: Local trial-based calibration without a predetermined global norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Linesearch Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking calibration using a computable local coupling test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given trial steps \(\tau_k>0\), \(\sigma_k>0\), a contraction factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and a margin \(\eta\in(0,1)\), compute the trial primal–dual update and its increments \(\Delta x\) and \(\Delta y\). Accept the trial when
\[2\langle K\Delta x,\Delta y\rangle\le \eta\bigl(\tau_k^{-1}\lVert\Delta x\rVert^2+\sigma_k^{-1}\lVert\Delta y\rVert^2\bigr).\]
Otherwise replace one or both trial steps by \(\rho\tau_k\) and \(\rho\sigma_k\), recompute the trial update, and repeat. Output the first accepted update and its stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking shrinks trial steps until the observed cross-coupling is dominated by the primal and dual metric terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted increments satisfy the displayed local metric-dominance test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits the leaf, but the increment test and step-reduction rule are variant-specific. A primary source is required to confirm the update definition, acceptance inequality, and termination guarantee.

children.title: Acceptance Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective criteria governing accepted parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bounds preventing accepted adaptive metrics from degenerating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An accepted adaptive stepsize sequence is safeguarded when there exist constants \(0<\underline\tau\le\overline\tau<\infty\), \(0<\underline\sigma\le\overline\sigma<\infty\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every accepted index \(k\),
\[\underline\tau\le\tau_k\le\overline\tau,\qquad \underline\sigma\le\sigma_k\le\overline\sigma,\qquad \tau_k\sigma_k\lVert K\rVert^2\le1-\varepsilon.\]
These checks exclude vanishing steps, unbounded steps, and loss of strict coupling admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safeguards bound accepted steps above and below while preserving a strict margin from the coupling boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted scalar metrics are uniformly coercive, bounded, and strictly admissible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: These are coherent sufficient safeguards, but adaptive splitting frameworks impose different boundedness, admissibility, and metric-variation conditions. An authoritative source for the intended framework is required.

children.title: Stepsize Criticality Boundary
children.top_down_role: Behavior near or beyond admissible scaling.

children.title: Boundary Stepsize Behavior
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior at critical admissibility thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Stepsize Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform metric coercivity at critical scalar coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded and let \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2=1\). Then the block metric
\[M=\begin{pmatrix}\tau^{-1}I&-K^*\\-K&\sigma^{-1}I\end{pmatrix}\]
is positive semidefinite but need not be strongly positive. If the norm of \(K\) is attained at unit vectors \(u\) and \(v\) with \(Ku=\lVert K\rVert v\), then \((\sqrt\tau u,\sqrt\sigma v)\) lies in the null space of \(M\). Hence convergence results requiring a uniformly coercive metric do not extend to equality without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At critical coupling the standard block metric can become singular, so strict-regime convergence arguments no longer apply automatically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\succeq0\) may be singular, and strict-admissibility convergence theory is inconclusive.

children.title: Supercritical Stepsize Instability
children.top_down_role: Oscillation or divergence beyond admissible scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Supercritical Stepsize Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar bilinear example exhibiting divergence beyond a supercritical threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(X=Y=\mathbb R\), \(K=1\), and the extrapolated primal–dual iteration
\[y_{k+1}=y_k+\sigma(2x_k-x_{k-1}),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-\tau y_{k+1}.\]
Writing \(q=\tau\sigma\), elimination of \(y_k\) gives
\[x_{k+1}=(2-2q)x_k+(q-1)x_{k-1}.\]
The characteristic polynomial is \(p(\lambda)=\lambda^2-(2-2q)\lambda-(q-1)\). For \(q>2\), it has a root with modulus greater than one; any initialization with a component in that eigendirection produces unbounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-dimensional bilinear primal–dual recurrence has an expanding eigenmode when its stepsize product exceeds two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(p)>1\), so generic iterates diverge geometrically.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence algebra supports divergence for q>2, although instability actually begins at a lower threshold for this recurrence. The notation rho(p) is also undefined because spectral radius applies to the companion operator, not directly to a polynomial. A source for the specific iteration is required before choosing the intended sharp formulation.

children.title: Stability Transition Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Changes in behavior as scaling crosses the admissibility boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability Transition Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local spectral characterization of stability changes in differentiable splitting dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(F_\alpha:Z\to Z\) be continuously differentiable near a fixed point \(z^\star\), and suppose \(F_\alpha(z^\star)=z^\star\). Writing \(e_k=z_k-z^\star\) and \(J(\alpha)=DF_\alpha(z^\star)\), the local dynamics satisfy
\[e_{k+1}=J(\alpha)e_k+o(\lVert e_k\rVert).\]
If \(\rho(J(\alpha))<1\), the fixed point is locally linearly attracting. If \(J(\alpha)\) has an eigenvalue of modulus greater than one, the fixed point is locally unstable. When \(J(\alpha)\) depends continuously on \(\alpha\), a transverse eigenvalue crossing from inside to outside the unit circle passes through a critical parameter at which an eigenvalue has modulus one; stability at that critical parameter is not determined by the linearization alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional differentiable iteration, eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle give local linear attraction, while an eigenvalue outside gives instability; a crossing through the unit circle marks a critical transition whose boundary behavior requires further analysis.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(F_\alpha\) is continuously differentiable near \(z^\star\) and satisfies \(F_\alpha(z^\star)=z^\star\).
\(J(\alpha)=DF_\alpha(z^\star)\) depends continuously on \(\alpha\) when a parameter transition is considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(J(\alpha))<1\) implies local linear attraction, an eigenvalue with modulus greater than one implies local instability, and a transverse unit-circle crossing identifies a critical stability transition.

children.title: Condat–Vũ Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual splitting with an additional smooth primal component.

knowledge_statements.title: Condat–Vũ Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic overrelaxed Condat–Vũ iteration for one smooth and two proximable convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_{x\in X} f(x)+h(x)+g(Kx),\]
where \(f,g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions and \(h\) is convex with \(L_h\)-Lipschitz gradient, choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2+\tau L_h/2<1\). Initialize \(x^0\in X\), \(y^0\in Y\), and set
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma Kx^k),\]
\[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\bigl(x^k-\tau(\nabla h(x^k)+K^*(2y^{k+1}-y^k))\bigr).\]
Return a primal–dual cluster point or stop when a prescribed residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condat–Vũ alternates a dual proximal step with a primal proximal-gradient step for a smooth-plus-composite convex objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration is the basic Condat–Vũ primal–dual splitting under strict scalar admissibility.

children.title: Combettes–Pesquet Primal–Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Product-space methods for multiple composite inclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Combettes–Pesquet Primal–Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space primal–dual splitting for finitely many linearly composed terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_{x\in X} f(x)+h(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(L_i x-r_i),\]
form \(Y=\prod_{i=1}^mY_i\), \(Lx=(L_i x)_i\), and \(G^*(v)=\sum_i\bigl(g_i^*(v_i)+\langle v_i,r_i\rangle\bigr)\). A product-space primal–dual step applies the separable resolvent
\[v_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_i g_i^*}\bigl(v_i^k+\sigma_i(L_i\bar x^k-r_i)\bigr)\]
for every \(i\), followed by a primal forward–backward update using \(\nabla h(x^k)+\sum_iL_i^*v_i^{k+1}\). Output primal and dual iterates when their inclusion residual is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method lifts multiple composite terms to a product space, enabling parallel dual proximal steps and one coupled primal update.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex and differentiable with Lipschitz gradient.
The block stepsizes make the induced product-space metric strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiple dual resolvents are separable across \(i\), while their adjoint contributions couple through the primal update.

notation.meaning: dual variable for the ith composite term

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-space interpretation fits the leaf, but the primal update, extrapolation rule for bar x^k, relaxation, and explicit admissibility condition are omitted. A primary source selecting a specific Combettes–Pesquet variant is required.

children.title: Loris–Verhoeven Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual forward–backward realization for linearly composed models.

knowledge_statements.title: Loris–Verhoeven Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual forward–backward scheme for a smooth term plus a linear composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\min_{x\in X} h(x)+g(Kx),\]
where \(h\) is convex with Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proximable. Given \(x^0\in X\), \(y^0\in Y\), define
\[\tilde x^k=x^k-\tau\bigl(\nabla h(x^k)+K^*y^k\bigr),\]
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}\bigl(y^k+\sigma K\tilde x^k\bigr),\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau\bigl(\nabla h(x^k)+K^*y^{k+1}\bigr).\]
Choose stepsizes in the convergence region of the selected Loris–Verhoeven variant, and stop when the primal–dual residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loris–Verhoeven uses forward gradient and adjoint steps together with a dual proximal correction for a linearly composed objective.
assumptions_latex: \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and has Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updates realize a primal–dual forward–backward treatment of \(\nabla h\), \(K\), and \(\partial g^*\).

notation.meaning: dual variable for the linear composite

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The named method has variant-sensitive update ordering and stepsize restrictions. Without a primary source, the displayed predictor-corrector iteration cannot reliably be identified as Loris–Verhoeven splitting.

children.title: Primal–Dual Three-Operator Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual realization of three-component splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Three-Operator Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-operator resolvent splitting applied to a primal–dual product-space inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z=X\times Y\) and consider the primal–dual inclusion
\[0\in A z+B z+C z,\]
where \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone with computable resolvents and \(C\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive. Choose \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), initialize \(w^0\in Z\), and iterate
\[x^k=J_{\gamma B}(w^k),\qquad y^k=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(2x^k-w^k-\gamma Cx^k\bigr),\]
\[w^{k+1}=w^k+y^k-x^k.\]
Stop when \(\lVert y^k-x^k\rVert\) is below tolerance and output \(x^k\), whose components are the primal and dual candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual product-space inclusion is split into two resolvent evaluations and one cocoercive forward evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\gamma<2\beta\) and the solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(y^k-x^k\) is the fixed-point residual of the three-operator primal–dual iteration.

children.title: Two-Block Separable Constraint Form
children.top_down_role: Canonical linearly coupled two-block model.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, convex functions.
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear, and \(c\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) is the canonical two-block separable linearly constrained model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional convex model underlying two-block ADMM.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The two-block separable constraint form is
\[
\underset{x\in X,\,z\in Z}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad f(x)+g(z)
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad Ax+Bz=c.
\]
Its feasible set is \(\{(x,z)\in X\times Z:Ax+Bz=c\}\). Separability means that the objective contains no term jointly depending on \(x\) and \(z\); interaction between the blocks occurs through the linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a sum of two convex block objectives while coupling the blocks only through one linear equality.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Separable Constraint Form

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian View
children.top_down_role: Alternating primal minimization and multiplier evolution.

assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the two-block separable constraint form hold.
\(\rho>0\), and each displayed subproblem attains a minimizer.
Initial values satisfy \(z^0\in Z\) and \(y^0\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed alternating minimizations followed by multiplier ascent constitute unscaled two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled augmented-Lagrangian formulation of exact two-block ADMM.

source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods
Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz-c\|^2.
\]
For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,z^k,y^k),\qquad
z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}L_\rho(x^{k+1},z,y^k),
\]
and update
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).
\]
The output after termination is the latest primal-multiplier triple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM alternately minimizes the augmented Lagrangian over each primal block and then performs a multiplier ascent update.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian View

children.title: Dual Operator-Splitting View
children.top_down_role: ADMM represented through a dual monotone inclusion.

assumptions_latex: The two-block convex problem has a primal-dual saddle point.
The conjugate-composition terms are proper and satisfy a qualification ensuring the stated subdifferential identities.
ADMM subproblems are solved exactly with \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two-block ADMM is representable, after the standard affine iterate correspondence, as Douglas-Rachford splitting for \(0\in\partial F(y)+\partial G(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-dual monotone-inclusion correspondence for exact convex ADMM.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Fenchel dual can be written
\[
\underset{y\in Y}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad F(y)+G(y),
\qquad F(y)=f^*(-A^*y)+\langle c,y\rangle,
\qquad G(y)=g^*(-B^*y).
\]
Its optimality inclusion is \(0\in\partial F(y)+\partial G(y)\). Douglas-Rachford splitting with stepsize \(\rho\) applies the fixed-point map
\[
T_{\mathrm{DR}}=I-J_{\rho\partial G}+J_{\rho\partial F}(2J_{\rho\partial G}-I).
\]
Under the standard affine identification of the Douglas-Rachford state with the ADMM multiplier and intermediate primal images, its iterates reproduce the exact two-block ADMM updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel dual yields a sum of two maximal monotone subdifferentials, and Douglas-Rachford splitting corresponds to ADMM under an affine iterate identification.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Operator-Splitting View

children.title: Consensus Forms
children.top_down_role: Variable-splitting structures centered on agreement across local copies.

assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 1\), and every \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A common global variable \(z\in X\) is introduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(x_i=z\) expose separable local objectives and enforce agreement through one global variable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-consensus reformulation with one local copy per objective term.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The centralized problem
\[
\underset{z\in X}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)
\]
has the equivalent consensus representation
\[
\underset{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z\in X}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad x_i-z=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Equivalence means that every feasible tuple has \(x_1=\cdots=x_m=z\), and projecting any feasible minimizer onto \(z\) gives a minimizer of the centralized problem, with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus reformulates a sum of functions using local variable copies constrained to equal one shared global variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Forms

children.title: Sharing Forms
children.top_down_role: Structures centered on shared resources or aggregate coupling.

assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 1\) is an integer, and \(X_1,\ldots,X_m,Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Introducing \(z_i=A_i x_i\) separates the local objectives from the aggregate coupling \(g(\sum_{i=1}^m z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharing reformulation for objectives coupled through an aggregate linear image.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sharing problem
\[
\underset{x_i\in X_i}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad
\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\right)
\]
has the equivalent constrained representation
\[
\underset{x_i\in X_i,\,z_i\in Y}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad
\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m z_i\right)
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad A_i x_i-z_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Eliminating the auxiliary variables \(z_i\) recovers the original objective exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sharing introduces local contribution variables so that only their aggregate enters the global convex cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharing Forms

children.title: Local–Global Coupling
children.top_down_role: Connections between parallel local subproblems and global coordination variables.

assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 1\) is an integer, and \(X_1,\ldots,X_m,Z,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(A_i:X_i\to Y_i\) and \(B_i:Z\to Y_i\) are linear, and \(c_i\in Y_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed constraints form a two-block coupling between the product local variable \(x=(x_i)_{i=1}^m\) and the shared global variable \(z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space form covering consensus and other star-coupled distributed models.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local-global coupling form is
\[
\underset{x_i\in X_i,\,z\in Z}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad
\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(z)
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad A_i x_i+B_i z=c_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
In product spaces, set \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), \(Ax=(A_i x_i)_{i=1}^m\), \(Bz=(B_i z)_{i=1}^m\), and \(c=(c_i)_{i=1}^m\). The model then has the canonical two-block constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\), while retaining separability of the local block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent local variables interact with one shared global variable through separate linear constraints, producing a two-block product-space model.
knowledge_statements.title: Local–Global Coupling

children.title: ADMM Residual-Multiplier Convergence
children.top_down_role: Feasibility, multiplier, and optimality convergence.

children.title: Feasibility Residual Convergence
children.top_down_role: Decay of primal constraint violation.

assumptions_latex: The two-block problem has a saddle point and \(f,g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Exact ADMM iterates are well defined for a fixed \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k\to0\), equivalently \(\|Ax^k+Bz^k-c\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic primal-feasibility conclusion for exact convex two-block ADMM.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\) be generated by exact two-block ADMM for
\[
\underset{x,z}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad f(x)+g(z)
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad Ax+Bz=c.
\]
If a primal-dual saddle point exists and every subproblem is attained, then the feasibility residual satisfies
\[
r^k:=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\longrightarrow 0.
\]
Thus every asymptotic cluster point of the primal iterates, when one exists, is feasible, although residual convergence alone does not imply convergence of the individual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard convex ADMM assumptions, violation of the linear coupling constraint converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Residual Convergence

children.title: Optimality Residual Convergence
children.top_down_role: Decay of residuals associated with block optimality.

assumptions_latex: The hypotheses for feasibility-residual convergence hold.
The dual residual is defined using the update order in which \(x\) is minimized before \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^{k+1}=\rho A^*B(z^{k+1}-z^k)\to0\), and the block stationarity defects vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity residual associated with the standard unscaled ADMM update order.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For exact two-block ADMM define
\[
s^{k+1}:=\rho A^*B(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
Under the stated convergence hypotheses,
\[
s^{k+1}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The subproblem optimality conditions and multiplier update give
\[
0\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^*y^{k+1}-s^{k+1},
\qquad
0\in\partial g(z^{k+1})+B^*y^{k+1}.
\]
Consequently, together with feasibility-residual convergence, the computable stationarity defects in the primal-dual optimality system vanish asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The change in the second block produces a dual stationarity residual that converges to zero under standard exact ADMM assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Residual Convergence

children.title: Multiplier Convergence
children.top_down_role: Limit behavior of the dual multiplier sequence.

assumptions_latex: The two-block convex problem admits at least one dual solution.
Exact fixed-penalty ADMM is well defined in finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
The associated Douglas-Rachford convergence hypotheses hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a dual solution \(y^\star\) such that \(y^k\to y^\star\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y^\star\) denote the nonempty set of dual optimal multipliers for the two-block problem. Under the exact finite-dimensional ADMM assumptions and the qualification needed for its Douglas-Rachford representation, there exists \(y^\star\in Y^\star\) such that
\[
y^k\longrightarrow y^\star.
\]
The limit therefore satisfies the dual stationarity conditions with some primal solution \((x^\star,z^\star)\):
\[
0\in\partial f(x^\star)+A^*y^\star,
\qquad
0\in\partial g(z^\star)+B^*y^\star.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the dual-splitting convergence hypotheses, ADMM multipliers converge to a dual optimal multiplier.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \((x^k,z^k)\) is bounded, the primal and stationarity residuals vanish, and \(y^k\to y^\star\). Closedness of convex subdifferential graphs implies that every cluster point \((\bar x,\bar z)\) satisfies
\[
A\bar x+B\bar z=c,
\qquad
0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^*y^\star,
\qquad
0\in\partial g(\bar z)+B^*y^\star,
\]
and hence is primal optimal. If \(Ax^k\) and \(Bz^k\) converge to optimal images and \(A\) and \(B\) are injective, then the corresponding primal blocks converge to the uniquely identified pair \((x^\star,z^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded iterates with vanishing optimality residuals have optimal cluster points; injective block maps can upgrade image convergence to variable convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Solution Recovery

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p^\star\) be the optimal value and let \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\) be the exact ADMM sequence. Under the standard saddle-point convergence hypotheses,
\[
p^k:=f(x^k)+g(z^k)\longrightarrow p^\star.
\]
This conclusion concerns the objective evaluated at the generally infeasible iterate pair \((x^k,z^k)\). It accompanies \(r^k\to0\) and does not by itself assert convergence of either primal block or uniqueness of a recovered primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective values of exact convex ADMM converge to the optimal value even when the individual primal iterates need not converge.

children.top_down_role: Regimes where residual convergence does not ensure full primal recovery.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\underset{x,z\in\mathbb R}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad 0
\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad 0x+z=0.
\]
Exact ADMM permits any minimizer in its \(x\)-subproblem. Choose \(x^k=(-1)^k\), \(z^k=0\), and \(y^k=0\). Then every update is admissible, while
\[
r^k=0,
\qquad
s^k=0
\]
for all \(k\). Nevertheless, \((x^k,z^k)\) does not converge. Thus vanishing feasibility and optimality residuals certify asymptotic conditions only in the observable linear images; recovery of variables requires additional identifiability, compactness, or uniqueness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free nullspace component can oscillate while every ADMM residual is identically zero, so residual convergence alone cannot recover primal variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Recovery Gap

children.title: Ergodic Gap Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Gap Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An iteration bound for the primal-dual gap of averaged two-block convex ADMM iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), and let \(\mathcal L(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle\). For the ergodic averages \(\bar x^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N x^k\), \(\bar z^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N z^k\), and \(\bar y^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N y^k\), suppose the standard ADMM energy estimate gives \(\mathcal L(\bar x^N,\bar z^N,y)-\mathcal L(x,z,\bar y^N)\le C(x,z,y)/N\) for every comparison point in a prescribed bounded set. Hence achieving gap at most \(\varepsilon>0\) requires at most \(N\ge\lceil C/\varepsilon\rceil\) iterations when \(C\) uniformly bounds \(C(x,z,y)\) on that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard ergodic primal-dual gap decreases as O(1/N), so an accuracy of epsilon requires O(1/epsilon) ADMM iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point of \(\mathcal L\) exists.
ADMM uses a fixed penalty \(\rho>0\) and exact subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{(x,z,y)}\{\mathcal L(\bar x^N,\bar z^N,y)-\mathcal L(x,z,\bar y^N)\}\le C/N\), and \(N=O(\varepsilon^{-1})\).

children.title: Ergodic Feasibility Complexity
children.top_down_role: Averaged constraint-violation progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Feasibility Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A telescoping residual bound for averaged two-block convex ADMM iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\) and let the multiplier update be \(y^k=y^{k-1}+\rho r^k\) with \(\rho>0\). For \(\bar x^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N x^k\) and \(\bar z^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N z^k\), telescoping gives \(A\bar x^N+B\bar z^N-c=(y^N-y^0)/(\rho N)\). If \(\|y^N-y^0\|\le D_y\) for all \(N\), then the ergodic feasibility violation is at most \(D_y/(\rho N)\). Thus feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is attained whenever \(N\ge\lceil D_y/(\rho\varepsilon)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded ADMM multipliers make the averaged constraint residual O(1/N), yielding O(1/epsilon) iteration complexity for ergodic feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The penalty parameter is fixed with \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|A\bar x^N+B\bar z^N-c\|\le D_y/(\rho N)\), so \(N=O(\varepsilon^{-1})\).

notation.meaning: Primal constraint residual at iteration k

children.title: Joint Certificate Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between gap quality and feasibility quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Certificate Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A joint interpretation of ergodic objective and feasibility bounds for convex ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\) be a saddle point, let \(p^\star=f(x^\star)+g(z^\star)\), and define \(r_N=A\bar x^N+B\bar z^N-c\). If a computable ergodic estimate supplies \(f(\bar x^N)+g(\bar z^N)-p^\star\le\delta_N\) and \(\|r_N\|\le\varepsilon_N\), then saddle-point optimality gives the complementary lower bound \(f(\bar x^N)+g(\bar z^N)-p^\star\ge-\|y^\star\|\varepsilon_N\). Consequently the pair \((\delta_N,\varepsilon_N)\) certifies both near-optimality and near-feasibility, while showing that objective values below \(p^\star\) can be explained by infeasibility of size \(\varepsilon_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility bound controls how far an infeasible averaged objective may fall below optimum; together with an upper gap bound it forms a joint certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The displayed objective and residual bounds are available for the ergodic iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\|y^\star\|\varepsilon_N\le f(\bar x^N)+g(\bar z^N)-p^\star\le\delta_N\) and \(\|r_N\|\le\varepsilon_N\).

children.title: Linear-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Strong convexity, smoothness, polyhedrality, and error-bound mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An error-bound mechanism that converts averaged-operator descent into local linear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a \(\theta\)-averaged fixed-point operator with \(0<\theta<1\), and consider \(w^{k+1}=Tw^k\). Suppose that near \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) the residual error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(w,\operatorname{Fix}T)\le\kappa\|w-Tw\|\) holds. Averagedness then yields \(\operatorname{dist}(w^{k+1},\operatorname{Fix}T)^2\le q^2\operatorname{dist}(w^k,\operatorname{Fix}T)^2\), where \(q^2=\max\{0,1-(1-\theta)/(\theta\kappa^2)\}<1\). For ADMM, strong convexity combined with suitable smoothness or rank conditions, and polyhedral or metric-subregularity assumptions, are standard routes for establishing such an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM becomes locally linearly convergent when its averaged fixed-point residual controls distance to the solution set; structural assumptions are used to establish that error bound.
assumptions_latex: The residual error bound holds on a neighborhood containing the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(w^{k+1},\operatorname{Fix}T)\le q\operatorname{dist}(w^k,\operatorname{Fix}T)\) for some \(q<1\).

children.title: Nonunique Solution Geometry
children.top_down_role: Limit-set structure when primal or dual solutions are nonunique.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Solution Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The primal and saddle solution sets underlying nonunique two-block convex ADMM limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear, let \(c\in Y\), and consider \(\min_{x\in X,z\in Z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with finite attained value \(p^\star\). Define \(\mathcal S_P=\{(x,z)\in X\times Z:Ax+Bz=c,\ f(x)+g(z)=p^\star\}\). For \(\mathcal L(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle\), define \(\mathcal S=\{(x,z,y)\in X\times Z\times Y:\mathcal L(x,z,y')\le\mathcal L(x,z,y)\le\mathcal L(x',z',y)\ \text{for all }(x',z',y')\in X\times Z\times Y\}\). Primal nonuniqueness means that \(\mathcal S_P\) contains at least two distinct points; primal-dual nonuniqueness means that \(\mathcal S\) contains at least two distinct points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal solution set contains all feasible optimal pairs, while the saddle set contains all primal-dual saddle points. Nonuniqueness means that the relevant set contains at least two distinct points.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The constrained problem has a finite attained value \(p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sets \(\mathcal S_P\) and \(\mathcal S\) represent primal and primal-dual solution geometry, respectively.

children.title: Partial Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence restricted to selected blocks, residuals, or images.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of identifiable images despite nonconvergence or nonuniqueness of raw primal components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s^k=(x^k,z^k)\) be a bounded sequence with \(\operatorname{dist}(s^k,\mathcal S_P)\to0\), and let \(M\) be a continuous linear map. If \(Ms=\bar m\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S_P\), then \(Ms^k\to\bar m\), even though \(s^k\) need not converge to a unique point. In ADMM this principle separates convergence of identifiable quantities, such as constraint images or residuals, from convergence of individual variables along null directions. Raw component convergence therefore requires additional uniqueness, injectivity, compactness, or regularity beyond convergence to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every solution has the same observable image, approaching the solution set forces that image to converge even when the underlying ADMM variables do not.
assumptions_latex: The continuous linear image \(M\) is constant on \(\mathcal S_P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ms^k\to\bar m\), while convergence of \(s^k\) itself is not implied.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound conditions that upgrade convergence of transformed ADMM variables to component convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(H\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, and let \(A:X\to H\) and \(B:Z\to H\) be linear. If there is \(\sigma_A>0\) such that \(\|Ah\|\ge\sigma_A\|h\|\) for every \(h\in X\), then \(Ax^k\to Ax^\star\) implies \(x^k\to x^\star\). Likewise, if there is \(\sigma_B>0\) such that \(\|Bv\|\ge\sigma_B\|v\|\) for every \(v\in Z\), then \(Bz^k\to Bz^\star\) implies \(z^k\to z^\star\). In finite dimensions, each lower-bound condition is equivalent to full column rank of the corresponding matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-column-rank constraint map converts convergence of a transformed component into convergence of the component itself.
assumptions_latex: The applicable map is bounded below by a positive constant, and its transformed iterate converges to the transformed target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The applicable lower-bound condition yields \(x^k\to x^\star\) or \(z^k\to z^\star\), respectively.

children.title: Solution-Selection Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of limiting solutions on initialization or parameter choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Selection Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A zero-objective consensus problem showing initialization-dependent ADMM solution selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z\in\mathbb R^n}0+0\) subject to \(x-z=0\). Every pair \((a,a)\), with \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), is optimal. For arbitrary \(z^0,u^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\rho>0\), scaled ADMM generates \(x^1=z^0-u^0\), \(z^1=z^0\), and \(u^1=0\), followed by \((x^k,z^k,u^k)=(z^0,z^0,0)\) for every \(k\ge2\). Therefore \((x^k,z^k)\to(z^0,z^0)\). Changing only \(z^0\) changes the selected primal solution although the optimization problem, penalty, and solution set are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a zero-objective consensus problem, scaled ADMM converges to the initial z-value; with a nonzero initial scaled multiplier, the stationary primal pair is reached at the second iteration.
assumptions_latex: Both objective functions are identically zero.
Scaled ADMM subproblems are solved exactly with \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,z^k)\to(z^0,z^0)\), so the selected solution depends on initialization.
