children.title: Relaxed ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using moderated reflection or update strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled two-block ADMM with relaxation applied to the first constraint image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear, let \(c\in Y\), and consider \(\min_{x\in X,z\in Z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). Given \(z^0\in Z\), \(u^0\in Y\), \(\rho>0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,2)\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\rho/2)\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2\}\). Form \(\widehat a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k)\), compute \(z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in Z}\{g(z)+(\rho/2)\|\widehat a^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2\}\), and set \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\widehat a^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold and return \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},\rho u^{k+1})\). The choice \(\alpha=1\) recovers ordinary scaled ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed ADMM replaces the newest first-block constraint image by a relaxed combination before the second-block and scaled-dual updates; alpha equal to one gives ordinary scaled ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each displayed subproblem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the relaxed-ADMM primal-dual iterate \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},\rho u^{k+1})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Overrelaxed ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The parameter regime in which relaxed ADMM extrapolates beyond the newest constraint image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_{x\in X,z\in Z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), use the relaxed-ADMM image \(\widehat a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k)\). The overrelaxed regime is \(1<\alpha<2\). In this regime, \(1-\alpha<0\), so \(\widehat a^{k+1}\) extrapolates from \(c-Bz^k\) through \(Ax^{k+1}\). The second-block and scaled-multiplier updates use this extrapolated image. For nonzero \(\alpha\), relaxation changes the fixed-point iteration but not the primal constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\) or the primal-dual saddle points represented by its fixed points. Any improvement relative to \(\alpha=1\) is problem-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overrelaxed ADMM uses a relaxation parameter strictly between one and two, extrapolating the newest first-block constraint image without changing the underlying constrained problem or its saddle points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and the constraint space are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, with compatible linear maps \(A\) and \(B\).
The relaxed-ADMM convention defining \(\widehat a^{k+1}\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat a^{k+1}\) is an extrapolation, while the target primal-dual saddle set is unchanged.

children.title: Relaxation Parameter Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Stable, critical, and unstable relaxation ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Parameter Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The open relaxation interval supporting the standard firmly-nonexpansive fixed-point convergence mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be firmly nonexpansive with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\), and consider \(w^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)w^k+\alpha Tw^k\). The standard relaxed fixed-point guarantee applies for \(0<\alpha<2\). At \(\alpha=0\), the iteration is \(w^{k+1}=w^k\) and a nonzero fixed-point residual is not reduced. At \(\alpha=2\), the iteration uses \(2T-I\), an unaveraged nonexpansive boundary; in the Douglas--Rachford convention this is the Peaceman--Rachford boundary, for which general convex convergence is not guaranteed. Values outside \([0,2]\) are likewise outside the baseline guarantee and require additional problem-specific structure. More generally, if \(T\) is only \(\theta\)-averaged, the standard relaxation interval is \(0<\alpha<1/\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a firmly nonexpansive splitting map, the standard relaxation range is strictly between zero and two: zero stagnates, and two reaches an unaveraged boundary without a general convex convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is firmly nonexpansive and has a nonempty fixed-point set.
No additional contraction, strong monotonicity, or problem-specific stabilization is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The baseline firmly-nonexpansive guarantee applies for \(0<\alpha<2\), but not generally at \(\alpha=0\), \(\alpha=2\), or outside this interval.

notation.meaning: Averagedness parameter in the general operator formulation

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block scaled ADMM with positive-semidefinite proximal regularizers in both subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear, let \(c\in Y\), and consider \(\min_{x\in X,z\in Z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). Given \(x^0\in X\), \(z^0\in Z\), \(u^0\in Y\), \(\rho>0\), and self-adjoint operators \(P:X\to X\) and \(Q:Z\to Z\) satisfying \(P\succeq0\) and \(Q\succeq0\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\rho/2)\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+(1/2)\|x-x^k\|_P^2\}\), then \(z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in Z}\{g(z)+(\rho/2)\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+(1/2)\|z-z^k\|_Q^2\}\), and set \(u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold and return \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},\rho u^{k+1})\). Setting \(P=0\) and \(Q=0\) recovers ordinary scaled ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal ADMM adds positive-semidefinite quadratic regularizers around both previous block iterates while retaining the usual scaled-multiplier update; zero metrics recover standard ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The proximal metrics are self-adjoint and satisfy \(P\succeq0\) and \(Q\succeq0\).
Each displayed subproblem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration produces a proximal-regularized ADMM sequence and reduces to standard scaled ADMM when \(P=0\) and \(Q=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block convex ADMM with the first quadratic penalty linearized and proximally majorized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) and \(g\) be proper closed convex functions and consider \(\min_{x,y} f(x)+g(y)\) subject to \(Ax+By=c\). Given \(\rho>0\), \(\tau_x>\rho\lVert A\rVert^2\), and \((x^0,y^0,\lambda^0)\), iterate
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\left\langle A^*\!\left(\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^k+By^k-c)\right),x-x^k\right\rangle+\frac{\tau_x}{2}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{g(y)+\langle\lambda^k,Ax^{k+1}+By-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax^{k+1}+By-c\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+By^{k+1}-c).
\]
Stop when prescribed primal- and dual-residual tolerances hold; otherwise output the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized ADMM replaces one coupled quadratic subproblem by a proximal first-order model, then performs the other ADMM minimization and the usual multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\) and \(B\) are bounded linear maps between finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\) is the next linearized-ADMM iterate.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the linear map A.
Proximal majorization parameter for the x-block.

children.title: Subproblem Simplification Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between easier block solves and stronger stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Simplification Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Majorization tradeoff for the linearized block of two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the linearized \(x\)-update, define \(P_x=\tau_x I-\rho A^*A\). If \(P_x\succeq0\), the update equals the exact augmented-Lagrangian \(x\)-subproblem with the additional proximal term \(\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_{P_x}^2\). Thus choosing scalar \(\tau_x\) can eliminate the coupled operator \(A^*A\) from the subproblem and reduce the step to evaluation of a proximal map of \(f\). Increasing \(\tau_x\) strengthens the majorization but shortens the effective primal step; choosing \(\tau_x<\rho\lVert A\rVert^2\) destroys this global quadratic-majorization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearization can turn a difficult coupled minimization into a proximal evaluation, but conservative majorization produces shorter steps; below the curvature threshold, the standard majorization guarantee fails.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a bounded linear map and \(\rho>0\).
The Euclidean proximal map of \(f\) is computationally available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_x\succeq0\) holds whenever \(\tau_x\geq\rho\lVert A\rVert^2\), yielding a valid proximal majorizer.

notation.meaning: Residual proximal metric after canceling augmented curvature.
Quadratic form given by the positive-semidefinite operator P_x.

children.title: Variable-Metric ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using iteration-dependent block metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block proximal ADMM whose primal metrics may vary with the iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,y}f(x)+g(y)\) subject to \(Ax+By=c\), choose self-adjoint positive-semidefinite operators \(P_k\) and \(Q_k\). From \((x^k,y^k,\lambda^k)\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\langle\lambda^k,Ax+By^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+By^k-c\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_{P_k}^2\right\},
\]
\[
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{g(y)+\langle\lambda^k,Ax^{k+1}+By-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax^{k+1}+By-c\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert y-y^k\rVert_{Q_k}^2\right\},
\]
followed by \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+By^{k+1}-c)\). Output the latest iterate when the selected residual test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric ADMM adds iteration-dependent quadratic proximal terms to the alternating primal updates while retaining the standard multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each displayed subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rules define one variable-metric ADMM step.

notation.meaning: The quadratic form given by the self-adjoint operator M.

children.title: Preconditioned ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using fixed metric scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-metric proximal ADMM for changing the geometry and conditioning of block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x,y}f(x)+g(y)\) subject to \(Ax+By=c\). Fix \(\rho>0\) and self-adjoint operators \(P\succeq0\) and \(Q\succeq0\). Preconditioned ADMM performs
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{L_\rho(x,y^k,\lambda^k)+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},
\qquad
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{L_\rho(x^{k+1},y,\lambda^k)+\frac12\lVert y-y^k\rVert_Q^2\right\},
\]
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+By^{k+1}-c),
\]
where \(L_\rho(x,y,\lambda)=f(x)+g(y)+\langle\lambda,Ax+By-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+By-c\rVert^2\). Stop by a prescribed residual criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned ADMM uses fixed positive-semidefinite proximal metrics to reshape the two primal subproblems without changing the constraint or multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is fixed-metric preconditioned ADMM; it is the constant-metric case of variable-metric ADMM.

children.title: Metric Admissibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Metric choices compatible with convergence and stable block solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Admissibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform coercivity and controlled variation conditions for variable metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequence of self-adjoint metrics \((M_k)_{k\geq0}\) is admissible under the uniformly coercive, summably varying regime when there exist constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\) and numbers \(\eta_k\geq0\) such that
\[
mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI,\qquad M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.
\]
For a linearized ADMM block with augmented curvature \(\rho A^*A\), admissibility additionally requires the effective proximal curvature to be nonnegative, for example \(M_k-\rho A^*A\succeq0\). These predicates exclude degenerating, unbounded, or persistently oscillating geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible metric stays uniformly positive and bounded, changes only by a summable relative amount, and dominates any augmented curvature removed by linearization.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_k\) is a self-adjoint operator on one finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
The Loewner order is used for metric comparisons.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities constitute a standard controlled-variable-metric admissibility regime.

children.title: Bregman ADMM
children.top_down_role: Non-Euclidean regularization of alternating subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM with non-Euclidean Bregman regularization in alternating primal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) and \(\psi\) be differentiable convex kernels on the interiors of their domains, with \(D_\phi(u,v)=\phi(u)-\phi(v)-\langle\nabla\phi(v),u-v\rangle\). For \(\min_{x,y}f(x)+g(y)\) subject to \(Ax+By=c\), choose \(\rho>0\) and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{L_\rho(x,y^k,\lambda^k)+D_\phi(x,x^k)\},
\]
\[
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{L_\rho(x^{k+1},y,\lambda^k)+D_\psi(y,y^k)\},
\qquad
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+By^{k+1}-c).
\]
All iterates must remain where the kernel gradients are defined; output the latest iterate at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman ADMM replaces Euclidean proximal regularizers in the two alternating subproblems by divergences generated by convex differentiable kernels.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\phi\) and \(\psi\) are differentiable convex kernels on the relevant iterates.
The displayed subproblems attain minimizers in the kernel domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration is Bregman-regularized two-block ADMM.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and non-Euclidean intent fit Bregman ADMM, but no citation is supplied. The precise kernel-domain assumptions and the convention for adding Bregman terms to both block updates require authoritative support. The statement also uses L_rho without explicitly defining it in the statement.

children.title: Stochastic ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants driven by random samples or stochastic estimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampled-gradient ADMM for an expected smooth loss coupled to a convex block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x,y}F(x)+g(y)\) subject to \(Ax+By=c\), where \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x;\xi)]\). Given a sample \(\xi_k\), an unbiased estimator \(G_k\) of \(\nabla F(x^k)\), and \(\tau_k>0\), set
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{\langle G_k,x-x^k\rangle+\langle\lambda^k,Ax+By^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+By^k-c\rVert^2+\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
then minimize the exact augmented Lagrangian over \(y\) at \(x^{k+1}\), and set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+By^{k+1}-c)\). Stop using a specified stochastic residual or iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic ADMM replaces the expected smooth loss by a sampled unbiased first-order model while retaining alternating constraint penalization and multiplier ascent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and differentiable, and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The conditional second moment of \(G_k-\nabla F(x^k)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rules define a sampled-gradient stochastic ADMM iteration.

notation.meaning: Stochastic gradient estimator at iteration k.
History available before sampling at iteration k.

children.title: Online ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants processing sequentially arriving data.

knowledge_statements.title: Online ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential ADMM using the current loss before the next data item arrives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), receive a proper convex loss \(f_t\) and consider the fixed coupling constraint \(Ax+By=c\). Given \((x_t,y_t,\lambda_t)\), choose \(\eta_t>0\) and compute
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f_t(x)+\langle\lambda_t,Ax+By_t-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+By_t-c\rVert^2+\frac{1}{2\eta_t}\lVert x-x_t\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
y_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{g(y)+\langle\lambda_t,Ax_{t+1}+By-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax_{t+1}+By-c\rVert^2\right\},
\]
then set \(\lambda_{t+1}=\lambda_t+\rho(Ax_{t+1}+By_{t+1}-c)\). Output the decision sequence or its average after the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online ADMM processes one convex loss per round, performs alternating constrained updates, and returns a decision sequence or averaged decision after the horizon.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_t\) and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The constraint operators and right-hand side are fixed over the horizon.
Each displayed minimization attains a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \((x_t,y_t,\lambda_t)\) is generated by online proximal ADMM.

notation.meaning: Convex loss revealed at online round t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Online ADMM, but no source is supplied. Online ADMM variants differ in whether the round-t decision precedes or follows revelation of f_t, and that timing affects both the algorithm and regret interpretation. children.title: Noise–Drift Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior under estimator noise, data drift, or changing objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise–Drift Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint stochastic-noise and moving-solution conditions for random-data splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be the algorithmic filtration, let \(e_k\) be the stochastic oracle error, and select a reference solution \(z_k^*\) for the problem at time \(k\). A summable-noise, bounded-drift regime is specified by
\[
\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0,
\qquad
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2\mathbb E[\lVert e_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty\quad\text{almost surely},
\qquad
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert z_{k+1}^*-z_k^*\rVert<\infty.
\]
For persistent-noise tracking, the first condition may remain valid while the variance sum or path-length sum is infinite; then exact asymptotic convergence is not implied by this regime, and performance must instead be expressed through a tracking or steady-state error criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convergence regimes require unbiased noise with summable weighted variance and a solution path of finite total drift; persistent noise or drift calls for tracking guarantees.
assumptions_latex: A measurable reference solution \(z_k^*\) exists at every time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three displayed predicates define the summable-noise, finite-drift regime; violating either summability predicate places the process in a tracking regime.

notation.meaning: Selected solution of the time-k problem.

children.title: Direct Multi-Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: Sequential extension to three or more blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Multi-Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Naive Gauss–Seidel extension of ADMM to three or more primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\geq3\), consider \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\). Given \(\rho>0\), direct multi-block ADMM sequentially computes, for \(i=1,\ldots,m\),
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\left\langle\lambda^k,r_i^k(x_i)\right\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r_i^k(x_i)\rVert^2\right\},
\]
where \(r_i^k(x_i)=\sum_{j<i}A_jx_j^{k+1}+A_ix_i+\sum_{j>i}A_jx_j^k-b\), followed by
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho\left(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\right).
\]
Stop by prescribed residual tolerances; no general convex convergence guarantee is part of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct multi-block ADMM minimizes the augmented Lagrangian sequentially over three or more blocks and then updates one multiplier, without an unconditional convex convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq3\) and every \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each sequential block subproblem attains a minimizer.
All spaces are finite-dimensional and each \(A_i\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gauss–Seidel sweep and multiplier step define direct multi-block ADMM.

notation.meaning: Constraint residual during block i of sweep k.

children.title: Multi-Block Divergence Phenomena
children.top_down_role: Failure of naive convex multi-block extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Block Divergence Phenomena
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete three-block feasibility instance exhibiting failure of direct convex multi-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider three scalar blocks with \(f_1=f_2=f_3=0\), right-hand side \(b=0\), and constraint
\[
A_1x_1+A_2x_2+A_3x_3=0,
\qquad
A_1=(1,1,1)^\mathsf T,
\quad A_2=(1,1,2)^\mathsf T,
\quad A_3=(1,2,2)^\mathsf T.
\]
The problem is convex and has the unique feasible point \((0,0,0)\). Nevertheless, for suitable nonzero initial primal and multiplier iterates, the unmodified three-block Gauss–Seidel ADMM iteration has a linear iteration operator with spectral radius greater than one and therefore does not converge. Hence convexity, exact block minimization, and full column rank of the assembled constraint matrix do not alone guarantee convergence of direct multi-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-scalar-block linear feasibility problem can make direct Gauss–Seidel ADMM diverge, despite convex objectives, exact subproblem solutions, and a uniquely feasible primal point.
assumptions_latex: Direct three-block ADMM uses one fixed penalty \(\rho>0\).
The block updates follow the order \(1,2,3\).
The initialization has a component in an unstable eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct three-block ADMM iterates fail to converge for this instance and suitable initialization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind is exactly appropriate for the divergence-phenomena leaf, and the displayed constraint matrix is nonsingular, so the claimed unique feasible point is plausible. Nevertheless, no source or inspected computation supports the crucial claim that this exact instance yields an iteration operator with spectral radius greater than one. The matrix, update convention, and instability claim require a precise counterexample citation.

children.title: Multi-Block Stabilization Family
children.top_down_role: Stabilization through block regularization and strengthened geometry.

children.title: Proximalized Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of multi-block convergence through proximal terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximalized Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of the sequential direct multi-block ADMM sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the multi-block problem \(\min\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=b\), choose self-adjoint \(P_i\succeq0\). During sweep \(k\), update each block sequentially by
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda^k,r_i^k(x_i)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r_i^k(x_i)\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x_i-x_i^k\rVert_{P_i}^2\right\},
\]
for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and then set
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho\left(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\right).
\]
The added terms make the block models more coercive and define a proximalized recovery candidate; convergence requires separate quantitative conditions on the metrics and coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximalized recovery adds positive-semidefinite quadratic regularizers to every sequential multi-block update, while leaving the common multiplier step unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each \(P_i\) is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite.
Every proximalized block subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration is proximalized sequential multi-block ADMM; stabilization is not asserted without additional metric conditions.

notation.meaning: Proximal stabilization metric for block i.
Partially updated constraint residual in block i.

children.title: Regularized Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery through strengthened block geometry or penalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov recovery of a canonical solution after regularizing a convex multi-block problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^m X_i\) be finite-dimensional, let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(C=\{x:\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\}\). Assume \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}F(x)\) is nonempty. For each \(\varepsilon>0\), define
\[
x_\varepsilon=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left(F(x)+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2\right).
\]
Then \(x_\varepsilon\) is unique and
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}x_\varepsilon=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}\lVert x\rVert.
\]
Thus a convergent splitting method applied to the regularized problems recovers the minimum-norm solution as the regularization vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive quadratic regularization makes each problem uniquely solvable; as the regularization vanishes, its solutions converge to the minimum-norm solution of the original problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and every \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(C\neq\varnothing\) and the original solution set \(S\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\to\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}\lVert x\rVert\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Solution set of the unregularized problem.

review_flags: Exact regularized-recovery theorem requires an authoritative locator specific to Tikhonov selection in constrained convex optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional Tikhonov selection claim is mathematically plausible, but the record provides no citation for its existence, uniqueness, and minimum-norm convergence theorem. The codomains of the operators A_i and the space containing b should also be stated when the record is sourced.

children.title: Sufficient Stabilization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ranges of stabilization strength supporting reliable convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Stabilization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-level sufficient condition covering proximal, damping, and metric stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(M\) be bounded and self-adjoint with \(M\succeq \mu I\) for some \(\mu>0\), and define \(\lVert z\rVert_M^2=\langle Mz,z\rangle\). A stabilized update map \(T:H\to H\) lies in a sufficient regime when, for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert_M^2\leq \lVert x-y\rVert_M^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\lVert (I-T)x-(I-T)y\rVert_M^2
\]
for all \(x,y\in H\). Equivalently, \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in the \(M\)-metric. If \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), the iteration \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) is asymptotically regular and converges weakly to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilization regime is sufficient when the resulting map is averaged in a uniformly positive metric; fixed-point iteration then converges weakly whenever fixed points exist.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and uniformly positive definite.
\(T\) satisfies the displayed averagedness inequality and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) converges weakly to an element of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\).

notation.meaning: Fixed-point set of the stabilized map.

children.title: Parallel Jacobian Multi-Block Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobi proximal ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stabilized simultaneous multi-block ADMM updates computed from a common previous iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=c\), define the block matrix \(P\) by
\[
P_{ii}=\gamma I,\qquad P_{ij}=-\rho A_{:,i}^{\top}A_{:,j}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
If \(\gamma\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^{\top}A)\), then \(P\succeq0\). Writing
\[
\mathbf L_\rho(x,u)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\langle u,Ax-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-c\|^2,
\]
Jacobi proximal ADMM computes simultaneously
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}}\left\{\mathbf L_\rho(x_i,x_{\ne i}^k,u^k)+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x_i-x_i^k\|^2\right\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,m,
\]
and then
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+\varphi\rho(Ax^{k+1}-c).
\]
The stated parameter requirements are \(\gamma\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^{\top}A)\) and \(\varphi\in(0,2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobi proximal ADMM updates all primal blocks simultaneously while holding every other block at its previous value. The chosen off-diagonal proximal terms cancel cross-block interactions, and sufficiently large diagonal stabilization makes the proximal matrix positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\succeq0\quad\text{and the primal update separates into simultaneous Jacobi block subproblems.}

children.title: Jacobian Multi-Block Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Multi-Block Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully simultaneous Jacobi ADMM for a linearly coupled separable convex program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given proper closed convex functions \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), solve \(\min\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\). Choose \(\rho>0\), initialize \((x^0,y^0)\), and select self-adjoint \(P_i\succeq0\). At iteration \(k\), compute every block concurrently by
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_i}\left\{f_i(u)+\left\langle y^k,A_i u+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b\right\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\lVert A_i u+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b\right\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert u-x_i^k\rVert_{P_i}^2\right\}.
\]
After all blocks finish, set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b)\). Stop when primal and dual residual tolerances are met; otherwise output the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobian multi-block ADMM minimizes every primal block simultaneously using only the previous blocks, then performs one multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Every displayed block subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule defines a synchronous Jacobi multi-block ADMM iterate \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).

children.title: Parallel Multi-Block Variants
children.top_down_role: Implementations organizing block subproblems for concurrent solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Multi-Block Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partially activated and relaxed parallel variants of a blockwise splitting map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=(T_1,\ldots,T_m):X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\to X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be a block splitting map. Initialize \(x^0\), and at iteration \(k\) choose a nonempty activation set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Compute \(\widetilde x_i^k=T_i(x^k)\) concurrently for \(i\in S_k\), and update
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_i^k+\omega_{i,k}(\widetilde x_i^k-x_i^k),&i\in S_k,\\x_i^k,&i\notin S_k,\end{cases}
\]
where \(\omega_{i,k}>0\). The fully synchronous variant uses \(S_k=\{1,\ldots,m\}\); cyclic, randomized, or minibatch variants use smaller sets. Stop at a prescribed fixed-point residual tolerance and output \(x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel variants evaluate selected block maps concurrently and may use full, cyclic, randomized, or minibatch activation with blockwise relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Each activated block evaluation \(T_i(x^k)\) is well-defined.
The activation and relaxation policies are specified before applying a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rule produces a relaxed parallel block-coordinate fixed-point iteration.

children.title: Parallel-Update Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Stabilization or correction mechanisms for simultaneous block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Update Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaging, relaxation, and fair activation safeguards for parallel block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive on a Hilbert product space with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). A synchronous safeguarded update is
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\lambda_k(Tx^k-x^k),\qquad 0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<1.
\]
For block-parallel execution, replace only activated coordinates and require bounded-delay fairness: there exists \(q\geq1\) such that every block is activated at least once among \(S_k,\ldots,S_{k+q-1}\). Under exact synchronous reads, the relaxed map \((1-\lambda_k)I+\lambda_kT\) is averaged; hence its fixed points equal those of \(T\), and the full-update sequence converges weakly to a fixed point. Partial or delayed variants additionally require a theorem matching their activation and delay model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe parallel updates use strict relaxation and fair block activation; delayed or partial execution needs bounds tailored to its activation model.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is nonexpansive and has a fixed point.
Relaxations remain in a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\).
For partial updates, every block is activated within each window of length \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For exact full updates, \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).

children.title: Fixed Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static change of metric for a maximal-monotone resolvent step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, and let \(M:H\to H\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and satisfy \(M\succeq\mu I\) for some \(\mu>0\). The fixed-preconditioned resolvent is
\[
J_{M^{-1}A}=(I+M^{-1}A)^{-1},
\]
and \(p=J_{M^{-1}A}x\) is equivalently characterized by
\[
M(x-p)\in Ap.
\]
Thus the preconditioner is constant across iterations and replaces the ambient inner product by \(\langle u,v\rangle_M=\langle Mu,v\rangle\). For \(A=\partial f\), the same step has the metric-proximal representation
\[
p=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in H}\left(f(z)+\frac12\lVert z-x\rVert_M^2\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive-definite preconditioner turns an ordinary resolvent into a resolvent and proximal map evaluated in one static metric.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and uniformly positive definite.
For the proximal representation, \(A=\partial f\) with \(f\) proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=J_{M^{-1}A}x\) if and only if \(M(x-p)\in Ap\), with the displayed proximal representation when \(A=\partial f\).

children.title: Iteration-Dependent Metrics

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Dependent Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform coercivity and summable variation for changing splitting metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((M_k)_{k\geq0}\) be bounded self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space. The sequence is an admissible controlled-variation metric family if there exist constants \(0<\mu\leq L<\infty\) and numbers \(\eta_k\geq0\) such that
\[
\mu I\preceq M_k\preceq LI,\qquad M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.
\]
Uniform bounds keep all metric norms equivalent to the ambient norm, while the summable relative-change condition prevents persistent metric expansion. These conditions provide the standard metric-control component of variable-metric quasi-Fejér and splitting convergence results; the operator update must separately satisfy the corresponding descent or averagedness hypothesis in each \(M_k\)-metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing metrics are controlled by uniform positive-definite bounds and summable relative growth; convergence still requires a compatible descent or averagedness condition.
assumptions_latex: The displayed uniform bounds and summable variation inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M_k)\) is a uniformly equivalent, summably varying metric sequence suitable for variable-metric convergence analysis.

children.title: Diagonal Metrics
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-separable scaling for primal, dual, or coordinate variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-separable positive metrics in finite-dimensional splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb{R}^n\), a diagonal splitting metric is a matrix
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n),\qquad d_j>0,
\]
which induces
\[
\langle x,y\rangle_D=\sum_{j=1}^n d_jx_jy_j,\qquad \lVert x\rVert_D^2=\sum_{j=1}^n d_jx_j^2.
\]
It is uniformly admissible when constants \(0<\mu\leq L<\infty\) satisfy \(\mu\leq d_j\leq L\) for every coordinate. For a separable function \(f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^n f_j(x_j)\), its metric proximal map separates coordinatewise:
\[
(\operatorname{prox}_f^D(x))_j=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}}\left(f_j(u)+\frac{d_j}{2}(u-x_j)^2\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal metric assigns a positive weight to each coordinate and preserves coordinatewise separability of proximal maps for separable functions.
assumptions_latex: For the proximal formula, \(f\) is proper, closed, convex, and coordinate-separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric norm and proximal subproblem decompose into independent scalar terms.

children.title: Block-Diagonal Metrics

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Diagonal Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly coercive product-space metrics that preserve independence among prescribed variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus X_m\) be a Hilbert product space. A uniformly positive block-diagonal metric is
\[
M=\operatorname{diag}(M_1,\ldots,M_m),
\]
where every \(M_i:X_i\to X_i\) is bounded and self-adjoint and there exist common constants \(0<\mu\leq L<\infty\) such that
\[
\mu I_i\preceq M_i\preceq L I_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
It induces
\[
\lVert x\rVert_M^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\langle M_i x_i,x_i\rangle.
\]
If \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is given by \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), where each \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, then
\[
\operatorname{prox}_f^M(x)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{f_1}^{M_1}(x_1),\ldots,\operatorname{prox}_{f_m}^{M_m}(x_m)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly positive block-diagonal metric weights each variable block independently and preserves blockwise proximal separability for proper lower-semicontinuous convex block-separable objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite product of Hilbert spaces.
Each \(M_i\) is bounded and self-adjoint, with common bounds \(\mu I_i\preceq M_i\preceq L I_i\) for constants \(0<\mu\leq L<\infty\).
For the proximal identity, each \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x\rVert_M^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\langle M_i x_i,x_i\rangle\), and the metric proximal map decomposes blockwise for block-separable \(f\).

notation.meaning: Uniformly positive metric operator on block i.
Identity operator on block space i.

children.title: Block Scaling Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of block metrics with operator coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Scaling Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-diagonal majorization condition for a linearly coupled quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m X_i\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be given by \(Ax=\sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i\), and choose \(M=\operatorname{diag}(M_1,\ldots,M_m)\) with self-adjoint blocks. For penalty \(\rho>0\), the block scaling is compatible with the coupling when
\[
M-\rho A^*A\succeq0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^m A_ih_i\right\rVert^2\leq\sum_{i=1}^m\langle M_ih_i,h_i\rangle
\]
for every \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\in X\). This inequality makes the block-diagonal quadratic a global majorant of the coupled penalty curvature, allowing a majorized surrogate to be minimized by independent block computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block scaling is compatible when its block-diagonal quadratic dominates the coupled penalty curvature, yielding a separable global majorant.
assumptions_latex: Each \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) is bounded and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\succeq\rho A^*A\), equivalently the displayed domination inequality holds for all block directions.

children.title: Degenerate Metric Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Metric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular positive-semidefinite metrics can destroy uniqueness of metric proximal steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(H=\mathbb{R}^2\), \(M=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), and \(f\equiv0\). Although \(M\succeq0\), it is not positive definite. For any \(x=(x_1,x_2)\), the nominal metric proximal problem is
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^2}\frac12\lVert z-x\rVert_M^2
=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^2}\frac12(z_1-x_1)^2
=\{(x_1,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.
\]
Hence the metric proximal operator is set-valued rather than a single-valued update, and \(M^{-1}\) does not exist. Positive semidefiniteness alone therefore does not ensure that a standard variable-metric resolvent or proximal iteration is well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular metric ignores nullspace directions, so even the proximal map of the zero function can be nonunique and the inverse metric undefined.
assumptions_latex: The metric is allowed to be positive semidefinite but singular.
The standard proximal update is required to be single-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nominal proximal solution set is \(\{(x_1,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\), so the update is not single-valued.

children.title: Indefinite Metric Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior under metrics lacking positive semidefiniteness.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Metric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative metric curvature can make a nominal proximal subproblem unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(H=\mathbb{R}^2\), \(M=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), and \(f\equiv0\). For any \(x=(x_1,x_2)\), the nominal metric proximal objective equals
\[
\frac12\lVert z-x\rVert_M^2=\frac12(z_1-x_1)^2-\frac12(z_2-x_2)^2.
\]
Setting \(z_1=x_1\) and letting \(\lvert z_2\rvert\to\infty\) sends this value to \(-\infty\). Consequently,
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^2}\frac12\lVert z-x\rVert_M^2=\varnothing.
\]
Thus an indefinite quadratic form need not define a norm or a well-posed proximal step; additional problem curvature sufficient to dominate its negative eigenspace would be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite metric contributes negative curvature, making even the zero-function proximal subproblem unbounded unless other curvature dominates every negative direction.
assumptions_latex: The metric is permitted to have a negative eigenvalue.
No additional strongly convex term compensates for the negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nominal metric proximal problem has infimum \(-\infty\) and no minimizer.

notation.meaning: Indefinite quadratic form, not a norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posedness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of metric coercivity can destroy uniqueness of variable-metric resolvent evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), and let \(M:H\to H\) be bounded and self-adjoint. A variable-metric resolvent evaluation at \(x\) seeks \(z\) satisfying \[M(x-z)\in Az.\] If \(A\) is maximally monotone and \(M\succeq mI\) for some \(m>0\), then this inclusion has exactly one solution for every \(x\in H\). Without coercivity, that conclusion is not guaranteed: if \(A=0\) and \(M\) is singular, every \(z=x+w\) with \(w\in\ker M\) solves the inclusion, so the metric resolvent is set-valued whenever \(\ker M\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive metric makes the variable-metric resolvent single-valued; a singular metric can produce infinitely many outputs even for the zero operator.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\succeq mI\) ensures unique resolvent evaluations, whereas singular \(M\) permits nonuniqueness for \(A=0\).

notation.meaning: The metric operator is uniformly positive with modulus m.

children.title: Averagedness Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Averagedness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step sizes and metric compatibility delimit averaged variable-metric forward maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb R\) with metric \(M=I\), and let \(B(x)=Lx\) for \(L>0\). The forward map with step size \(\gamma>0\) is \(T=I-\gamma B\), hence \(T(x)=(1-\gamma L)x\). A scalar linear map \(x\mapsto qx\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) only if \(-1<q\le 1\). Consequently, \(T\) is averaged when \(0<\gamma L<2\), but it is not averaged when \(\gamma L\ge 2\). Thus even a positive metric cannot preserve averagedness once the metric-scaled step exceeds its cocoercivity range; an indefinite metric additionally fails to define the Hilbert norm required by averagedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward step loses averagedness at the sharp scalar threshold gamma times L equals two; indefinite metrics do not even define the required norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is averaged for \(0<\gamma L<2\) and is not averaged for \(\gamma L\ge 2\).

notation.meaning: Slope and cocoercivity-scale parameter of B.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Prox Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two non-Euclidean prox evaluations implement an extragradient correction for monotone variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(X^*\) and pairing \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\). Let \(C\subset X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(U\subset X\) be an open convex set containing \(C\), and let \(h:U\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and strictly convex. Define \(D_h(u,v)=h(u)-h(v)-\langle\nabla h(v),u-v\rangle\) for \(u,v\in U\), and let \(F:C\to X^*\). Given \(x_k\in C\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), compute \[y_k\in\arg\min_{y\in C}\left\{\gamma_k\langle F(x_k),y\rangle+D_h(y,x_k)\right\},\] and then compute \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\left\{\gamma_k\langle F(y_k),x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\right\}.\] The second evaluation uses the predicted point \(y_k\), thereby providing the corrected-forward interface characteristic of Mirror-Prox.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-Prox performs a predictive Bregman prox step and then a corrected Bregman prox step, evaluating the field first at the current point and then at the prediction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space and \(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set containing \(C\).
\(F:C\to X^*\) is single-valued, and both displayed minimization problems attain solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update consists of a Bregman prediction \(y_k\) followed by a corrected Bregman step using \(F(y_k)\).

children.title: Summable Deterministic Errors
children.top_down_role: Perturbations controlled through cumulative error budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Deterministic Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convergence of perturbed averaged fixed-point iterations under an absolute cumulative error budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). Let \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/(2\alpha))\), suppose \(\lambda_k\in[\varepsilon,1/\alpha-\varepsilon]\), and let \(e_k\in H\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\). Starting from any \(x_0\in H\), define \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k\bigl(Tx_k+e_k-x_k\bigr).\] Then \(\lVert Tx_k-x_k\rVert\to0\), and \((x_k)\) converges weakly to a point of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\). If \(H\) is finite-dimensional, the convergence is in norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed averaged iteration converges to a fixed point when its deterministic evaluation errors have finite weighted total magnitude and the relaxation parameters remain uniformly inside the admissible interval.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(T:H\to H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) such that \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\), and \(\lVert Tx_k-x_k\rVert\to0\).

notation.meaning: Set of fixed points of T.
Deterministic evaluation error at iteration k.

children.title: Relative Error Criteria
children.top_down_role: Inexactness measured relative to local iterate or subproblem scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Error Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An inexact resolvent is accepted when its inclusion residual is small relative to its displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), let \(x\in H\), and let \(\lambda>0\). An approximate resolvent pair \((y,v)\in H\times H\) satisfies the relative error criterion with parameter \(\sigma\in[0,1)\) when \[v\in Ay\quad\text{and}\quad \lVert \lambda v+y-x\rVert\le \sigma\lVert y-x\rVert.\] The left side is the resolvent-equation residual, while the right side scales tolerance by the computed step. For \(\sigma=0\), the criterion reduces to the exact resolvent relation \(x-y=\lambda v\) with \(v\in Ay\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate resolvent is accepted when its equation residual is at most a fixed fraction of the step length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,v)\) is acceptable exactly when \(v\in Ay\) and \(\lVert\lambda v+y-x\rVert\le\sigma\lVert y-x\rVert\).

children.title: Residual Error Criteria
children.top_down_role: Inexactness measured through computable residual quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Error Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute acceptance criterion for an inexact resolvent equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), and fix an input \(x\in H\), parameter \(\lambda>0\), and tolerance \(\epsilon\ge0\). A pair \((y,v)\in H\times H\) is an \(\epsilon\)-residual-accurate evaluation of the resolvent of \(A\) at \(x\) when \[v\in Ay\quad\text{and}\quad \lVert y+\lambda v-x\rVert\le\epsilon.\] The computable vector \(r=y+\lambda v-x\) measures violation of the exact equation. If \(\epsilon=0\), then \(y=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}x\) whenever the resolvent is single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact resolvent is accepted when a compatible graph pair violates the exact resolvent equation by no more than an absolute tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is equivalent to \(v\in Ay\) and \(\lVert y+\lambda v-x\rVert\le\epsilon\).

children.title: Local Error Calibration
children.top_down_role: Relationships between accepted error levels and local progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Error Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent tolerances are scaled by locally observable update magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact splitting step at iteration \(k\), let \(r_k\) denote its computable defining-equation residual and let \(s_k\ge0\) be a local scale available before acceptance, such as \(s_k=\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert\). Given \(\eta_k\ge0\) and an absolute safeguard \(\delta_k\ge0\), accept the step when \[\lVert r_k\rVert\le \delta_k+\eta_k s_k.\] This calibration is local because the permitted error depends only on current-step quantities. The purely relative rule is recovered with \(\delta_k=0\); the purely absolute residual rule is recovered with \(\eta_k=0\). Convergence claims require separate conditions controlling the resulting sequence of accepted errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local calibration combines an absolute tolerance with a tolerance proportional to a current, observable step scale.
assumptions_latex: \(r_k\) is a computable residual and \(s_k\ge0\) is observable at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step is accepted when \(\lVert r_k\rVert\le\delta_k+\eta_k s_k\).

children.title: Stochastic Error Models

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Error Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional bias and variance describe random perturbations in splitting evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real separable Hilbert space, and let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space with filtration \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\). A stochastic splitting-error model is a sequence of square-integrable \(H\)-valued random variables \((e_k)_{k\ge0}\) such that \(e_k\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable. Relative to the pre-evaluation history \(\mathcal F_k\), define \[b_k=\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k],\qquad \xi_k=e_k-b_k.\] Then \[e_k=b_k+\xi_k\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\quad\text{almost surely}.\] A conditional second-moment budget consists of nonnegative \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable random variables \(\sigma_k^2\) satisfying \[\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_k^2\quad\text{almost surely}.\] The processes \((b_k)\) and \((\sigma_k^2)\) encode conditional bias and fluctuation magnitude, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic splitting error can be decomposed, relative to the information available before its evaluation, into a predictable conditional bias and a conditionally mean-zero fluctuation with a conditional second-moment budget.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real separable Hilbert space and \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) is a filtration on \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_k=b_k+\xi_k\), where \(b_k=\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\), \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_k^2\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Conditional bias given the pre-evaluation history.
Information available before the iteration-k random evaluation.

children.title: Martingale-Difference Errors
children.top_down_role: Conditionally centered perturbations with filtration-based control.

knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditionally centered perturbations relative to the algorithmic information filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real separable Hilbert space, and let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry a filtration \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\). Let \(e_k:\Omega\to H\) be Bochner integrable and \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable for every \(k\ge0\). The sequence \((e_k)_{k\ge0}\) is a martingale-difference error sequence relative to \((\mathcal F_k)\) when \[\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\quad\text{almost surely for every }k\ge0.\] Consequently, for every bounded \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable \(H\)-valued random variable \(u_k\), \[\mathbb E[\langle u_k,e_k\rangle]=0.\] Thus the current error has no predictable first-order component given the pre-evaluation history, although its conditional second moment may be nonzero or iteration-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A martingale-difference error is an integrable Hilbert-space-valued perturbation whose conditional mean is zero given all information available before the current random evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real separable Hilbert space and \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) is a filtration.
Each \(e_k:\Omega\to H\) is Bochner integrable and \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) almost surely for every \(k\ge0\), and \(\mathbb E[\langle u_k,e_k\rangle]=0\) for every bounded \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable \(H\)-valued random variable \(u_k\).

notation.meaning: Algorithmic history before error e_k is realized.
Random splitting error at iteration k.

children.title: Probabilistic Error Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Long-run effects of random error sequences on convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment accumulation for stochastic perturbations in a filtered splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge 0}\) be a filtration and let \((e_k)_{k\ge 0}\) be square-integrable Hilbert-space-valued errors satisfying \(\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), where \(e_k\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\). For deterministic coefficients \((a_k)\), the accumulated error \(S_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}a_ke_k\) satisfies \[\mathbb E\lVert S_n\rVert^2=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}a_k^2\mathbb E\lVert e_k\rVert^2.\] Consequently, if \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2\mathbb E\lVert e_k\rVert^2<\infty\), then \((S_n)\) is Cauchy in \(L^2\), so probabilistic errors accumulate according to their weighted variances rather than their absolute magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally mean-zero splitting errors accumulate in mean square through the sum of weighted variances; finite total weighted variance gives an L2-convergent cumulative perturbation.
assumptions_latex: \((a_k)\) is deterministic and square-weighted variances are summable for the convergence conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\lVert S_n\rVert^2=\sum_{k<n}a_k^2\mathbb E\lVert e_k\rVert^2\), and summability implies convergence of \((S_n)\) in \(L^2\).

notation.meaning: Information available before the kth error is realized.
Random splitting error at iteration k.
Weighted cumulative error through iteration n minus one.

children.title: Biased-Error Convergence Boundary

children.title: Persistent Bias
children.top_down_role: Nonvanishing systematic perturbations in splitting evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent conditional bias in an additive-error splitting model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an adapted perturbed iteration \(x_{k+1}=T_kx_k+e_k\) on a Hilbert space, with filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\). Its conditional bias is \(b_k=\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\). The error process has persistent bias along an infinite index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) if there exists \(\beta>0\) such that \(\lVert b_k\rVert\ge\beta\) almost surely for every \(k\in K\). It is asymptotically persistently biased if \(b_k\to b\) almost surely or in norm for some nonzero vector \(b\). Thus the systematic component of the perturbation does not vanish even when its centered component does.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A splitting error is persistently biased when its conditional mean stays bounded away from zero infinitely often, or converges to a nonzero vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent bias means \(\inf_{k\in K}\lVert\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\rVert\ge\beta>0\) for some infinite \(K\), or asymptotically \(b_k\to b\ne0\).

children.title: Residual Error Floors
children.top_down_role: Positive limiting levels for residual or certificate values.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Error Floors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Steady-state distance bound for a contractive splitting map under uniformly bounded additive errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a contraction on a Hilbert space with modulus \(q\in[0,1)\) and unique fixed point \(x^\star\). If \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k+e_k\) and \(\lVert e_k\rVert\le\varepsilon\) for all \(k\), then for every \(k\ge0\), \[\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert\le q^k\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert+\frac{1-q^k}{1-q}\varepsilon.\] Hence \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert\le\varepsilon/(1-q)\). To guarantee distance at most \(\delta>\varepsilon/(1-q)\), it suffices that \(q^k\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert\le\delta-\varepsilon/(1-q)\); no such uniform guarantee follows from this bound when \(\delta\le\varepsilon/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction with errors bounded by epsilon approaches an error floor epsilon divided by one minus the contraction factor; iteration complexity applies only above that floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert\le\varepsilon/(1-q)\).

notation.meaning: Unique fixed point of the exact operator.

children.title: Neighborhood Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence to a solution neighborhood rather than an exact solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setwise convergence consequence of the contractive bounded-error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in[0,1)\) on a Hilbert space, let \(x^\star\) be its fixed point, and generate \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k+e_k\) with \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert\le\varepsilon\). Then \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert\le\frac{\varepsilon}{1-q}.\] Equivalently, for every \(r>\varepsilon/(1-q)\), there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in\overline B(x^\star,r)\) for all \(k\ge K\). Thus bounded asymptotic error yields eventual residence in every strictly larger neighborhood, without asserting convergence to a single point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under contraction and asymptotically bounded errors, all sufficiently late iterates remain in any ball whose radius exceeds epsilon divided by one minus the contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(r>\varepsilon/(1-q)\), eventually \(x_k\in\overline B(x^\star,r)\).

notation.meaning: Closed radius-r ball centered at the exact fixed point.

children.title: Exact-Recovery Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conditions preventing exact residual decay or exact solution recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Recovery Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar boundary showing that constant nonzero bias precludes recovery of the exact fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(q\in[0,1)\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\). On \(\mathbb R\), let \(T(x)=qx\), whose unique fixed point is \(x^\star=0\), and consider \(x_{k+1}=qx_k+b\). Then \[x_k=q^kx_0+\frac{1-q^k}{1-q}b\longrightarrow\frac{b}{1-q}.\] Consequently, this family converges to the exact fixed point \(x^\star\) if and only if \(b=0\); every constant bias \(b\ne0\) moves the limit away from \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the scalar contraction mapping x to qx, exact recovery occurs exactly when the constant additive bias is zero; every nonzero constant bias shifts the limit to b divided by one minus q.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x^\star\) if and only if \(b=0\); for \(b\ne0\), \(x_k\to b/(1-q)\ne x^\star\).

notation.meaning: Exact fixed point, equal to zero.

children.title: A Priori Parameter Policies

knowledge_statements.title: A Priori Parameter Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-independent calibration from global operator constants known before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parameterized family of splitting maps \((T_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}\), an a priori parameter policy is a mapping \(P:\mathcal I\to\Theta^{\mathbb N_0}\), where \(\mathcal I\) contains only problem data and global regularity constants available before iteration zero. For \(I\in\mathcal I\), the method fixes the entire schedule \(P(I)=(\theta_k)_{k\ge0}\) before execution and does not use subsequently observed iterates or residuals. The policy is admissible when \(\theta_k\in\Theta_{\mathrm{safe}}(I)\) for every \(k\ge0\), where \(\Theta_{\mathrm{safe}}(I)\) is the parameter region under which the selected splitting operator has the required averagedness, nonexpansiveness, or contractivity property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An a priori policy fixes the complete parameter schedule from globally known problem information before iteration begins and keeps every parameter in a certified safe region.
assumptions_latex: \(I\in\mathcal I\) is available before iteration zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(I)=(\theta_k)_{k\ge0}\) is fixed before execution and satisfies \(\theta_k\in\Theta_{\mathrm{safe}}(I)\) for every \(k\ge0\).

children.title: Backtracking Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric step reduction until a local majorization test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), an initial trial step \(\widehat\gamma_k>0\), and \(\rho\in(0,1)\), set \(\gamma=\widehat\gamma_k\) and compute \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x_k-\gamma\nabla f(x_k))\). While \[f(z)>f(x_k)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),z-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert z-x_k\rVert^2,\] replace \(\gamma\) by \(\rho\gamma\) and recompute \(z\). Upon acceptance, set \(x_{k+1}=z\) and \(\gamma_k=\gamma\). Stop according to a prescribed residual or iteration criterion and return the latest accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking repeatedly shrinks a trial proximal-gradient step until the smooth term satisfies a local quadratic upper-model test, then accepts the resulting iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and has locally Lipschitz gradient on the tested segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted pair \((x_{k+1},\gamma_k)\) satisfies the displayed local majorization inequality.

notation.meaning: Geometric contraction factor for rejected trials.

knowledge_statements.title: Linesearch Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General trial-generation and acceptance framework for locally calibrated splitting parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a finite or countable ordered trial set \(\Gamma_k\subset(0,\infty)\). For each \(\gamma\in\Gamma_k\), compute a trial point \(z(\gamma)=T_\gamma x_k\) and an observable merit pair \((M_k(z(\gamma)),R_k(z(\gamma)))\). Accept the first trial satisfying \[M_k(z(\gamma))\le M_k(x_k)-c\,R_k(z(\gamma))^2\] for a prescribed \(c>0\); set \(x_{k+1}=z(\gamma)\) and \(\gamma_k=\gamma\). If no trial is accepted, report linesearch failure or invoke a separately specified fallback. Stop when \(R_k(x_k)\) meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linesearch tests ordered splitting parameters and accepts the first trial producing a prescribed merit decrease relative to a computable residual; otherwise it reports failure or uses a fallback.
assumptions_latex: Each trial map \(T_\gamma\), merit value \(M_k\), and residual \(R_k\) is computable.
The trial ordering and fallback behavior are fixed before the search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted step satisfies \(M_k(x_{k+1})\le M_k(x_k)-cR_k(x_{k+1})^2\).

notation.meaning: Ordered candidate parameter set at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Acceptance Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable local conditions preventing unsafe acceptance of a trial splitting step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current iterate \(x_k\), trial point \(z=T_\gamma x_k\), merit function \(M_k\), residual \(R_k\), and admissible interval \([\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\), a safeguarded acceptance predicate is \[\mathsf{Accept}_k(z,\gamma)\iff \gamma_{\min}\le\gamma\le\gamma_{\max},\quad M_k(z)\le M_k(x_k)-cR_k(z)^2,\quad \lVert z-x_k\rVert\le D_k,\] where \(c>0\) and \(D_k>0\) are prescribed. A local calibration policy may accept a trial only when this predicate holds; rejection triggers another trial or a declared fallback. The three clauses respectively enforce parameter admissibility, measurable progress, and bounded displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local safeguard accepts a trial only if its parameter is admissible, it yields sufficient merit decrease, and its displacement stays within a prescribed bound.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\), \(R_k\), and \(\lVert z-x_k\rVert\) are evaluable for every trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires simultaneous parameter, progress, and displacement safeguards.
review_flags: This is a generic safeguard predicate; the taxonomy does not specify which concrete splitting merit and residual are intended.
A source is needed to select a canonical acceptance test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate is internally consistent, but its three-clause safeguard is an uncited design choice rather than a canonical local acceptance condition.

children.title: Residual-Balancing Policies
children.top_down_role: Adaptive scaling based on competing residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Balancing Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative rescaling driven by imbalance between two competing normalized residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given positive residuals \(r_k^{(p)}\) and \(r_k^{(d)}\), scaling parameter \(\tau_k>0\), imbalance threshold \(\mu>1\), and multiplier \(\eta>1\), update \[\tau_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\eta\tau_k,&r_k^{(p)}>\mu r_k^{(d)},\\ \tau_k/\eta,&r_k^{(d)}>\mu r_k^{(p)},\\ \tau_k,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Optionally project the result onto a prescribed interval \([\tau_{\min},\tau_{\max}]\). The residuals must be normalized to comparable units. The policy outputs the new scaling for the next splitting step and stops only through the parent algorithm's residual or iteration criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual balancing multiplies or divides a splitting scale when one normalized residual dominates the other, and leaves the scale unchanged when they are comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_{k+1}\) is increased, decreased, or retained according to the displayed residual-ratio test.

children.title: Unknown-Constant Calibration Family
children.top_down_role: Policies reducing dependence on unknown global constants.

children.title: Parameter-Free Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies avoiding externally supplied global calibration constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online calibration requiring no user-supplied numerical regularity or tuning constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a splitting family \((T_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}\), a parameter-free policy is an online rule \(\theta_k=P_k(H_k)\), where \(H_k=(x_0,\ldots,x_k;R_0,\ldots,R_k)\) is the observed history, such that the user supplies no numerical Lipschitz, cocoercivity, strong-monotonicity, noise, or target-accuracy constant to determine \(\theta_k\). Any internal constants are fixed universally as part of the algorithm. The policy remains parameter-free only if initialization and safeguarding are also determined from observed quantities or universal constants, rather than hidden problem-dependent tuning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter-free policy selects every splitting parameter from observed history and universal built-in constants, without user-provided regularity, noise, accuracy, or tuning values.
assumptions_latex: The history \(H_k\) contains only quantities observable by iteration \(k\).
All internal numerical constants are fixed independently of the problem instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_k=P_k(H_k)\) requires no user-supplied problem-dependent numerical constant.

notation.meaning: Observable algorithmic history through iteration k.

review_flags: Parameter-free has incompatible conventions across optimization literature.
A source is required to determine whether universal built-in constants and stopping tolerances are permitted locally.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Conventions for “parameter-free” differ over built-in constants, initialization, safeguards, and stopping tolerances, so this definition requires a source fixing the intended convention.

children.title: Universal Calibration Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies adapting across multiple smoothness or regularity regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Calibration Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive calibration matching known-rate dependence without prior knowledge of the governing regularity constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal P_L)_{L>0}\) be problem classes indexed by an unknown regularity constant \(L\), and let \(B(N,L,I_0)\) be a benchmark error bound after \(N\) oracle calls when \(L\) is known. A calibration policy is universal over these classes if it does not receive \(L\) as input and there exist numerical constants \(C\ge1\) and \(c\ge1\), independent of \(L\), \(N\), and the instance, such that every instance in \(\mathcal P_L\) satisfies \[\operatorname{Err}(x_N)\le C\,B(\lfloor N/c\rfloor,L,I_0).\] Thus adaptation loses at most constant factors in accuracy and oracle budget relative to calibrated performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal policy does not know the governing regularity constant yet matches the corresponding known-constant benchmark up to instance-independent constant factors in error and oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: Each instance belongs to some class \(\mathcal P_L\) with finite but unknown \(L\).
\(B\) is a fixed known-constant benchmark under the same oracle and error conventions.
The adaptive policy receives no value of \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Err}(x_N)\le C B(\lfloor N/c\rfloor,L,I_0)\) for universal constants \(C,c\).

notation.meaning: Problem class governed by regularity constant L.
Known-constant benchmark error after N oracle calls.
Specified objective, residual, or distance error criterion.

review_flags: Universality depends on the intended problem scale, oracle model, and allowable logarithmic overhead.
The supplied locators do not determine the chapter's intended universal-calibration guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constant-factor benchmark formulation is not a universal convention; some universal methods permit logarithmic overhead or use different oracle and regularity models. A source must determine the intended guarantee.

children.title: Unknown-Constant Robustness
children.top_down_role: Performance when global operator constants are unavailable or inaccurate.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Constant Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness of adaptive splitting policies to unavailable problem constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a problem class indexed by an unknown constant \(c>0\), and let \(B_N(c,z^0)\) be a residual bound attainable when \(c\) is known. A parameter-selection policy \(\Pi\) is unknown-constant robust on \(\mathcal P\) if its parameters at iteration \(k\) depend only on observed iterates and oracle outputs, never on the numerical value of \(c\), and there exist constants \(C\geq 1\) and \(q\geq 0\), independent of \(c\), \(N\), and the instance, such that its output satisfies \[R_N(\Pi)\leq C\bigl(1+\log(N+1)\bigr)^q B_N(c,z^0)\] for every instance in \(\mathcal P\) and every \(N\geq 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is robust to an unknown constant when it never uses that constant numerically yet matches the known-constant residual bound up to uniform constants and logarithmic factors.
assumptions_latex: \(c>0\) is fixed for each instance but unavailable to the policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_N(\Pi)\leq C(1+\log(N+1))^qB_N(c,z^0)\) uniformly over the problem class.

notation.meaning: residual or certificate produced after N iterations by policy Pi
benchmark guarantee available when the constant is known

children.title: Best-Iterate Residual Rates
children.top_down_role: Guarantees for the most favorable observed iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Residual Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Picard iteration of an averaged operator with a nonempty fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and suppose \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). For \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k\), define \(r_k=x^k-Tx^k\) and \(d_0=\operatorname{dist}(x^0,\operatorname{Fix}T)\). Then, for every integer \(N\geq0\), \[\min_{0\leq k\leq N}\|r_k\|^2\leq \frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)(N+1)}d_0^2.\] Thus an iterate with fixed-point residual at most \(\varepsilon\) occurs within \(N+1\geq \alpha d_0^2/((1-\alpha)\varepsilon^2)\) operator evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among the first N+1 iterates of an averaged fixed-point iteration, one has residual of order one over square root of N+1.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged on a Hilbert space, with \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\leq k\leq N}\|x^k-Tx^k\|\leq \sqrt{\alpha/(1-\alpha)}\,d_0/\sqrt{N+1}\).

notation.meaning: fixed-point residual x^k minus T x^k
initial distance to the fixed-point set
